features.summary: Foundations setup now runs on one Salesforce Go page; marketing items have their own page. Added: access is controlled only by the Foundations license, and missing licenses can be added via Update Licenses.
features.recommendation: If you have Salesforce Foundations, open Setup > Salesforce Foundations and check on the new Go page which features are turned on. If the page shows a Prerequisites section, recommended licenses are missing; add them with Update Licenses.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with a Salesforce Foundations license: Setup > Salesforce Foundations.

explainer.what: Salesforce Foundations is a bundle of core features that many customers get at no extra cost. Its settings now sit on one clear page instead of being scattered across Setup.
explainer.benefit: You see at a glance what is turned on and what is still missing.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Features you already turned on stay active.

features.title: Salesforce in Claude: Create and Update Records for 46 More Objects
features.summary: Salesforce in Claude can now create and update records for 46 more objects, including quotes, orders, carts, promotions, notes, and email templates. The same validations as in Lightning apply.
features.recommendation: If you use Salesforce in Claude with write access, the new objects are available without further setup. Decide whether users should be able to change quotes, orders, or email templates from Claude, and adjust permissions if needed.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with Claude Enterprise and record write enabled in the Salesforce MCP server.

explainer.what: Salesforce in Claude lets you work with Salesforce data directly in the AI assistant Claude. Claude can now also create and change quotes, orders, or notes, not just read them.
explainer.benefit: More work can be done right in the chat without switching between apps.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. If you don't use the feature, nothing changes.

features.title: CMS MCP Server: Semantic Search for Text-Based and Multilingual Content
features.summary: The Content Read-Only MCP server now finds CMS content of any type and language via semantic search. The new tool search_digital_content is added, and search_electronic_media now supports multilingual media.
features.recommendation: If you connect AI assistants to Salesforce CMS, activate the content-readonly MCP server, deploy the CMS Base data kit, and turn on or update the search indexes. Currently available only in Developer Edition, scratch orgs, and sandboxes.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you use Salesforce CMS with AI assistants; available in Developer Edition, scratch orgs, and sandboxes.

explainer.what: AI assistants can search content in the Salesforce content system through an interface. Until now they only found English images and media; now they also find text like newsletters or landing pages in any language.
explainer.benefit: Content teams find the right material faster, even across languages.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The feature is optional.

features.title: Salesforce Builder Central: Build Apps and Agents by Describing Them (Beta)
features.summary: In Builder Central you describe an app or agent in plain language; a Build Agent plans it, builds it, and shows the changes. You validate in a temporary preview org and then deploy to a sandbox.
features.recommendation: If you have Foundations or Agentforce 1, try Builder Central in a Developer sandbox (enable it from the App Launcher or Setup). Review the generated metadata carefully before deploying, then follow your normal release process.
features.checkHint: Only available with Salesforce Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions.

explainer.what: Instead of configuring an application step by step, you describe in a sentence what you need, for example an app to manage loaner devices. An AI proposes a plan, builds it, and shows a preview.
explainer.benefit: First drafts take minutes instead of days, and business teams can make ideas tangible faster.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. This is an optional beta feature.

features.title: Quick Pages: Create Custom Pages with Natural Language (Beta)
features.summary: With Quick Pages you describe a page, for example for pipeline reviews or meeting prep, and an agent builds a React UI grounded in your Salesforce data. Pages can be shared; viewers see only data allowed by their own access.
features.recommendation: If your org runs on Hyperforce and has Foundations, assign the Create and View Quick Pages (Beta) permission set to a small pilot group and have them build, for example, a pipeline overview. During the beta, pages are read only and the AI features are free.
features.checkHint: Only available with Salesforce Foundations and hosting on Hyperforce.

explainer.what: You write, for example, show me all open deals of my team with totals per month, and an AI turns it into a ready-made overview page in Salesforce that you can share with colleagues.
explainer.benefit: Overviews for meetings or presentations without developers and without exporting to Excel.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. This is an optional beta feature.

features.title: Turn On and Configure Fundraising with an AI Agent
features.summary: An AI agent can turn on Fundraising, assign permission sets, create a default gift designation, and set up optional features. The skill runs through the Headless 360 MCP Server (Beta).
features.recommendation: If you're setting up Fundraising, use the nonprofit-fundraising-configure skill (Agentforce Vibes, or Claude Code with the Headless 360 MCP Server) in a sandbox first. Caution: Fundraising and Person Accounts can't be turned off once enabled, so review the agent's plan carefully before confirming.

explainer.what: Setting up donation management in Salesforce used to take many clicks across different Setup pages. Now you can tell an AI assistant to set up Fundraising, and it does the steps after asking you to confirm.
explainer.benefit: Initial setup is faster and less error-prone.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Setup through the regular Setup pages still works.

features.title: Salesforce in Claude: CRM Context Directly in Claude (Beta)
features.summary: Through an MCP connection and pre-built skills, Claude surfaces deal health, pipeline risk, and account context from your org. Corrected: editions; added: the Needs Approval setting for write actions.
features.recommendation: If you use Claude Enterprise, turn on the Headless 360 MCP Server and set up the External Client App. Note: by default the feature is available to everyone in the org; limit access with a permission set if needed and review existing profile permissions before rollout.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with Claude Enterprise.

explainer.what: Sales reps who work with the AI assistant Claude can ask there which of their deals are at risk and get the answer from live Salesforce data.
explainer.benefit: Less switching between apps and fewer reports to pull by hand. Existing Salesforce permissions still apply.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The connection only exists once an admin sets it up.

features.title: Setup with Agentforce: Query 10 More Setup Objects
features.summary: The Setup agent can answer natural-language questions about 10 more Setup objects, including ApexClass, ApexPage, PlatformEventChannel, and restriction rules. Read access only.
features.recommendation: If you use Setup with Agentforce, ask the Setup agent about Apex classes, Visualforce pages, or platform event channels instead of searching the lists manually. No setup is required.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with Setup with Agentforce (Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions).

explainer.what: Admins can ask about Salesforce settings in a chat, for example which Apex classes exist. The assistant now knows ten more areas.
explainer.benefit: Admins find technical information faster without clicking through Setup pages.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The extension arrives automatically.

features.title: Setup with Agentforce Requires Data Cloud Again
features.summary: Data Cloud is again a required, not optional, prerequisite for enabling Setup with Agentforce. The September note saying Data Cloud was no longer required has been withdrawn.
features.recommendation: If you planned to roll out Setup with Agentforce without Data Cloud, include Data Cloud enablement in your plan or postpone the rollout. From your org's Winter '27 upgrade (rolling from October 2026), Data Cloud is a prerequisite.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you want to use Setup with Agentforce (Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions).

explainer.what: The AI assistant for admins in Setup needs the Data Cloud data platform after all. An earlier announcement that it works without it no longer applies.
explainer.benefit: Clarity for planning: if you want to introduce the assistant, you know which prerequisite you need.
explainer.ifNothing: Without Data Cloud, Setup with Agentforce can't be enabled. Otherwise nothing changes.

features.title: Hyperforce Available in More Regions
features.summary: Hyperforce runs on AWS in 18 countries (including Germany and Switzerland) and on Google Cloud in North America. More products, such as Data 360, Marketing Cloud, and Event Log Objects, are available in additional countries.
features.recommendation: For information only. If data residency matters to you, check the Trust and Compliance documentation for which products are available on Hyperforce in your country.

explainer.what: Hyperforce is the infrastructure that runs Salesforce in the data centers of large cloud providers. It is now available in more countries and for more products.
explainer.benefit: More choice about the country where your data is stored, which can matter for data protection rules.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Hyperforce Generally Available on Google Cloud in North America
features.summary: Since November 1, 2026, Hyperforce on Google Cloud Platform is generally available in the United States, with most Sales Cloud and Service Cloud features. Salesforce manages infrastructure placement.
features.recommendation: Only relevant for orgs in the United States. If you use IP allowlisting, add the Hyperforce GCP addresses from ip-ranges.salesforce.com, including email. If contracts rule out specific cloud providers, contact your Salesforce account team.
features.checkHint: Only relevant for orgs in the United States, especially with IP allowlisting.

explainer.what: Salesforce can now run customer orgs in the United States on Google as well as Amazon. If your firewall only allows specific Salesforce addresses, you need to know the new ones.
explainer.benefit: Customers with cloud-provider requirements get an alternative.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing for orgs outside the United States. With strict firewall rules, connections or emails could otherwise be blocked.

features.title: Hyperforce Information Bundled in Salesforce Help
features.summary: Hyperforce guidance from scattered knowledge articles is now in one Salesforce Help bundle, covering topics such as migrations, networking, and data residency.
features.recommendation: For information only. If a Hyperforce migration is coming up, use the Hyperforce Overview in Salesforce Help as your starting point.

explainer.what: Guidance about the Salesforce infrastructure Hyperforce used to be spread across many separate articles. Now there's one connected guide with a table of contents.
explainer.benefit: If you're preparing a move, you find everything in one place.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: GraphQL API: Block Guest Access, Get Lookup and Default Values
features.summary: Admins can block unauthenticated guest user access to GraphQL API (rolling out from late October 2026). Existing orgs with guest access since May 2026 stay open. New fields lookupValues and recordCreateDefaults are also available.
features.recommendation: You have an active Experience Cloud site. In Setup > UI API Access Controls, check whether guest users really need GraphQL API, and block access if not. The setting only takes effect once the feature has rolled out to your org.
features.checkHint: Setup > UI API Access Controls: check guest access to GraphQL API.

explainer.what: Through websites built on Salesforce, such as customer portals, visitors who aren't logged in can send technical queries to Salesforce. You can now switch off this access for one specific interface.
explainer.benefit: Smaller attack surface: anonymous visitors can no longer reach data that was accidentally shared with them through this interface.
explainer.ifNothing: Existing orgs keep their current guest access. If guest permissions are too generous, that risk remains.

features.title: Experience Builder: Offer Multiple Flow Approval Processes per Record
features.summary: The Request Approvals component on detail pages in Aura and LWR sites can reference up to 10 flow approval processes. Logged-in site visitors pick the right process when submitting.
features.recommendation: You have an active site and {automation.flowApprovals|flow approval process|flow approval processes}. If partners or customers submit records for approval in the portal, add the Request Approvals component to the detail page and reference the relevant processes.

explainer.what: In a partner or customer portal, users can submit, for example, a discount request for approval. If there are several approval paths, they can now choose the right one directly.
explainer.benefit: Fewer requests submitted the wrong way and less rework for the back office.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing portals keep working unchanged.

features.title: Migrate Up to 100 Subscriber Orgs per Day from 1GP to 2GP
features.summary: Push upgrades that migrate subscribers from 1GP to 2GP packages now support up to 100 subscriber orgs per day, up from 5.
features.recommendation: Only relevant for AppExchange partners: if you have a 2GP package converted from 1GP, replan the migration of your customer orgs with the new daily limit.
features.checkHint: Only relevant for ISV partners with their own managed packages.

explainer.what: Software vendors that sell Salesforce add-ons are moving their packages to newer technology. They can now move many more customers per day.
explainer.benefit: Vendors finish the move faster.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing for regular customer orgs.

features.title: Update CMS Search Indexes for AI Search Across All Content Types
features.summary: The CMS Base data kit search indexes now include all CMS content types (except brand and taxonomy terms) instead of only English media. The indexes have to be rebuilt for this.
features.recommendation: If you use Salesforce CMS with Data 360 and the CMS Base data kit is already deployed, uninstall and reinstall the search indexes and turn them on again under After You Deploy. Otherwise, deploy it from Setup > CMS Base Data Kit.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you use Salesforce CMS: Setup > CMS Base Data Kit.

explainer.what: For AI features to find content in the Salesforce content system, they need a search index. It now also covers text and multilingual content, but has to be rebuilt once.
explainer.benefit: AI searches find far more of your content, not just English images.
explainer.ifNothing: Search stays limited to the previous, smaller scope.

features.title: Create and Manage Brands in All Enhanced CMS Workspaces
features.summary: The Brand content type is available in all enhanced CMS workspaces, not only in Marketing Cloud Next. Added: a dark mode color palette for SLDS 2 (in general workspaces) and guidance on brand usage.
features.recommendation: If you build Multi-Framework apps with Agentforce Vibes, define your brand colors and fonts once as a brand in CMS and add a dark mode palette if needed. In general workspaces, a brand applies only to Multi-Framework apps.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with enhanced CMS workspaces.

explainer.what: A brand stores your visual identity: colors, fonts, buttons. Until now this existed only in marketing; now it also works for apps you build yourself, including a variant for dark display.
explainer.benefit: Your own apps look consistent with your brand without styling every detail separately.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Trialforce: Verify Email-Sending Domains (Deadline Nov 10, 2026)
features.summary: Trialforce branded email sets need verified sending domains to create new Trialforce source orgs and templates. For existing templates, without verification by November 10, 2026, a substitute sender address is used.
features.recommendation: Only for AppExchange partners using Trialforce: in your Trialforce management org, open Setup > Branding > Email Sets and check the Verified Email Domain column. Verify missing domains with a DKIM key or an authorized email domain. Sets already verified via DKIM are covered automatically.
features.checkHint: Only relevant for ISV partners with a Trialforce management org: Setup > Branding > Email Sets.

explainer.what: Software vendors send emails from trial environments (Trialforce) under their own name. Salesforce now requires proof that they really own the sending domain.
explainer.benefit: Fewer spoofed senders and better email deliverability.
explainer.ifNothing: After November 10, 2026, emails from existing templates go out with a neutral Salesforce substitute address, and new source orgs and templates can't be created.

features.title: See Which Infrastructure Your Salesforce Edge Network Uses
features.summary: My Domain now shows whether your org's Edge Network runs on Hyperforce AWS, Hyperforce GCP, or Salesforce first-party data centers.
features.recommendation: For information only. If you maintain network or firewall rules, check in Setup > My Domain which infrastructure your Edge Network uses or will use.

explainer.what: The Edge Network speeds up access to Salesforce by routing requests through nearby servers. Setup now shows which provider runs those servers.
explainer.benefit: IT can plan network rules more precisely.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Lifecycle Center: Validate Deployments Before Promoting
features.summary: A validate-only deployment finds deployment errors, Apex test failures, and code coverage gaps without changing the target org. After a successful validation, you can complete the promotion within 10 days without rerunning tests.
features.recommendation: If you use Lifecycle Center, choose Validate only with an Apex test option under Promote Stage, especially before production deployments. That way you fix errors upfront and shorten the actual deployment in the maintenance window.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you use Lifecycle Center for deployments.

explainer.what: Before changes reach production, you can now do a dry run. It shows all errors but doesn't change anything yet.
explainer.benefit: Fewer failed deployments and shorter maintenance windows because tests don't run twice.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Deployments keep working as before.

features.title: Update Your Mobile Publisher App: Refresh Token Rotation Is Coming
features.summary: Salesforce is enabling Refresh Token Rotation (RTR) against stolen credentials and token replay. Users on older app builds are then signed out and can't log back in until the app is updated.
features.recommendation: If you have a Mobile Publisher app for an Experience Cloud site, build a new version after October 21, 2026 and publish it to the App Store and Google Play. Ask your users to install the update before RTR is enabled for your app.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you have your own Mobile Publisher app for an Experience Cloud site in the app stores.

explainer.what: Your own app in the app store, based on a Salesforce customer portal, keeps users signed in with a key. For security, Salesforce will now regularly swap that key; old app versions can't handle that.
explainer.benefit: Stolen sign-in keys quickly become worthless.
explainer.ifNothing: As soon as Salesforce turns this on for your app, users on the old version are signed out and can't get back in.

features.title: Metadata API: Sharing Reasons for Standard Objects and New MarketingObject Type
features.summary: Added: the SharingReason metadata type now supports custom sharing reasons on standard objects with a share object, such as Account and Opportunity. The new MarketingObject type stores marketing reference data.
features.recommendation: You have {dev.apexClasses|custom Apex class|custom Apex classes}. If you share records with Apex managed sharing, check whether custom sharing reasons on Account or Opportunity improve traceability, and version them through the Metadata API.

explainer.what: Developers can define in code why a colleague may see a customer record. Until now this reason could only be named on custom objects; now it also works on standard objects like accounts.
explainer.benefit: It stays clear why someone has access, and sharing can be removed in a targeted way.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Create Native Mobile Apps with Agentforce (GA)
features.summary: Agentic Mobile Apps is generally available: describe an app in plain language, Agentforce builds the screens, and you publish it to the App Store and Google Play and analyze usage.
features.recommendation: If you're planning your own employee or customer app, enable Agentic Mobile Apps in Setup and build a prototype. For customer apps, pick an existing Experience Cloud site as the basis. Decide upfront who owns the app store accounts and the publishing process.
features.checkHint: Only available with Salesforce Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions.

explainer.what: Building your own phone app used to take months. Now you describe what the app should do, for example field reps log visit reports, and an AI builds a first draft that you adjust and publish.
explainer.benefit: Custom apps for employees or customers become much faster and cheaper.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The feature is optional.

features.title: Connect External MCP Servers with Per-User Credentials
features.summary: Users can call external MCP servers through OAuth 2.0 with their own credentials instead of a shared system-to-system connection. Register the server with an external credential that uses per-user authentication.
features.recommendation: If your agents use external MCP servers through a shared technical connection, check whether a per-user external credential fits better. Each user then accesses the external system only with their own permissions, and access is traceable per person.

explainer.what: AI agents in Salesforce can use tools from other systems. Until now they often signed in there with a shared account. Now each user can sign in with their own account.
explainer.benefit: Nobody sees more through the agent than they're allowed to see in the other system.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing connections keep working.

features.title: Create Custom Salesforce-Hosted MCP Servers via API
features.summary: The API Catalog Connect REST API lets you create custom Salesforce-hosted MCP servers that expose tools and prompts to Agentforce and other MCP clients, including in automated workflows.
features.recommendation: If you provide custom MCP servers for agents, create them through the API Catalog Connect REST API so you can roll them out by script and reproducibly between sandbox and production.

explainer.what: MCP servers are interfaces that let AI assistants use Salesforce functions. Developers can now set up these interfaces with an API call instead of clicking through screens.
explainer.benefit: Setups can be automated and repeated identically across environments.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Setup through the user interface still works.

features.title: Digital Wallet: New Home Page, Side Navigation, and Billing View
features.summary: The Digital Wallet app has a new home page as a central overview of consumption and investment, a left-side navigation instead of many tabs, and now also shows invoices and contracts.
features.recommendation: Whoever owns licenses and consumption in your company should take a look at the new home page in the Digital Wallet app. The home page requires the View Consumption permission; check that the right people have it.

explainer.what: Digital Wallet is the Salesforce app that shows how much of your purchased licenses and consumption allowances is used. It now has a clear home page and also shows invoices and contracts.
explainer.benefit: Costs and contracts in one place, without asking your account manager.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Digital Wallet: Enhanced Consumption Analytics Dashboard
features.summary: The Consumption Analytics Dashboard shows cumulative year-to-date consumption, lists all sources and usage types instead of only the top 10, and adds a Consumption by Feature view, for example for Agentforce Coworker and Prompt Builder.
features.recommendation: If you use consumption-based features like Agentforce or Prompt Builder, check in Digital Wallet > Consumption Analytics which features consume the most, and set up a regular review if needed.

explainer.what: Some Salesforce features, especially AI, are billed by consumption. A dashboard now shows more precisely which feature consumed how much.
explainer.benefit: Cost drivers become visible early, before your allowance runs out.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. You just miss out on better cost transparency.

features.title: Digital Wallet: Export License Utilization to CSV
features.summary: License utilization data can be exported from Digital Wallet to a CSV file, for example for analysis in a BI tool.
features.recommendation: You use {licenses.salesforceUsed|Salesforce license|Salesforce licenses}. Before your next contract renewal, export license utilization from Digital Wallet > License Utilization and check whether unused licenses can be reduced. This requires the View License Utilization permission.

explainer.what: You can now download a table showing how many of your purchased Salesforce licenses are actually used.
explainer.benefit: A good basis for contract negotiations and for finding unused licenses.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Lifecycle Center: Import Jira Work Items
features.summary: After connecting a Jira workspace once, you can search, filter, and bulk-import Jira work items into Lifecycle Center, with a permanent link back to the original.
features.recommendation: If you use Lifecycle Center and Jira, turn on the Jira integration under Lifecycle Center Home > Manage Features (Lifecycle Center Admin permission) and import items with Import from Jira instead of entering them twice.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you use Lifecycle Center and Jira.

explainer.what: Many teams manage requirements in Jira and Salesforce changes in a separate tool. Jira tasks can now be pulled in directly instead of being retyped.
explainer.benefit: Less double entry and clear traceability of which change belongs to which requirement.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Catalan and Basque User Interface Languages Generally Available
features.summary: Catalan and Basque are generally available as user interface languages for Service Cloud and Agentforce Public Sector. Missing translations fall back to Spanish; Translation Workbench translations stay untouched.
features.recommendation: Only relevant if you have Catalan or Basque speaking users: review the translations briefly in a sandbox and adjust the language settings in Setup > Language Settings if needed.

explainer.what: Salesforce is now officially available in Catalan and Basque, starting with the customer service area.
explainer.benefit: Employees in these regions can work in their native language.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Review Updated Standard Label Translations (Including German)
features.summary: Salesforce changed translations of some standard object, tab, and field names in many languages, including German in Winter '27. More languages received new or updated translations in October 2026.
features.recommendation: Download the list of changes from the knowledge article Review Winter '27 Updated Label Translations and check whether training materials, reports, or guides are affected. To keep a previous label, rename the tab or field in Setup.

explainer.what: Salesforce improved the German (and other) names of some standard fields and tabs. A field may suddenly be called something slightly different.
explainer.benefit: More accurate terms in the user interface.
explainer.ifNothing: The new names appear anyway. Users may be confused if training materials still show the old terms.

features.title: Security Center: Track Security Threats with Security Investigations
features.summary: Detected threats such as credential stuffing, login anomalies, or API anomalies are tracked as investigations from first alert to remediation. A remediation plan guides the steps; test events help you practice.
features.recommendation: You have the Security Center add-on. Open the new Security Investigations tab, decide who handles investigations (View Security Center Pages or Manage Security Center permission), and run through the process once with a test event.

explainer.what: When Salesforce detects suspicious activity, such as mass login attempts with stolen passwords, it now creates a case with clear steps: check, contain, fix. A dashboard shows where each case stands.
explainer.benefit: Security incidents are handled in a structured, traceable way instead of getting lost in emails.
explainer.ifNothing: Detections keep running, but you don't use the guided handling process.

features.title: Security Center: Customize Remediation Plans and Steps for Investigations
features.summary: Security Investigations comes with predefined remediation plans, for example for credential stuffing, login anomalies, and session hijacking. Plans and steps can be versioned, reordered, and refined with test events.
features.recommendation: You have the Security Center add-on. Review the predefined plans in Security Center > Configuration > Security Investigations, adapt them as a new version to your incident process (for example, who gets notified), and test them with a test event before activating.

explainer.what: For typical attacks there are ready-made checklists of what to do. You can adapt them to your own processes, such as who is notified first.
explainer.benefit: In an emergency everyone knows what to do, and nothing gets forgotten.
explainer.ifNothing: Salesforce's standard checklists apply unchanged.

features.title: MFA for Previously Exempt Users: Exemption Is Ending (Release Update)
features.summary: For orgs with an extension for the Waive Multi-Factor Authentication for Exempt Users permission: once it expires, these users must use MFA too, and privileged users a phishing-resistant method. The API field PermissionsBypassMFAForUiLogins is removed.
features.recommendation: Check the enforcement date in Setup > Release Updates (a one-time 90-day extension is possible). Find out who has Waive Multi-Factor Authentication for Exempt Users and have them register an MFA method, even with SSO. Remove references to PermissionsBypassMFAForUiLogins from code, metadata, and integrations.
features.checkHint: Only applies to orgs with an extension for exempt users: check Setup > Release Updates.

recommendationVariants.text: Check the enforcement date in Setup > Release Updates. {security.usersWithoutMfaMethod|active user doesn't|active users don't} have an MFA method yet. Check whether previously exempt users are among them and have them register a method beforehand. Also remove references to PermissionsBypassMFAForUiLogins from code and metadata.

explainer.what: Some users were explicitly exempt from providing a second proof at login, such as an app or a passkey. This exemption is now ending.
explainer.benefit: Even the last accounts without a second factor are protected against stolen passwords.
explainer.ifNothing: After the deadline, affected users without a method can't easily get in. Code that uses the removed field can block package installs.

features.title: Banner Warns 30 Days Before MFA and Step-Up Extensions Expire
features.summary: Orgs with an extension for MFA, phishing-resistant MFA, or step-up authentication on report exports see a banner 30 days before expiry with links to the release updates. Visible only to users with broad permissions.
features.recommendation: When the banner appears, click View updates and work through the linked release updates. Note: if you dismiss the banner, it stays hidden, so also put the enforcement dates from Setup > Release Updates in your calendar.
features.checkHint: Only applies to orgs with an MFA or step-up extension: check Setup > Release Updates.

explainer.what: Some companies got a postponement from Salesforce for stricter login rules. A banner now reminds admins 30 days before it ends.
explainer.benefit: Deadlines don't get forgotten.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. If you dismiss the banner, you have to track the deadlines yourself.

features.title: Overview: Review and Comply with Upcoming Security Requirements
features.summary: Hub page for upcoming security requirements: access controls, email verification, and connected apps and external client apps using OAuth. Updated with the release updates for orgs with an MFA or step-up extension.
features.recommendation: Go through Setup > Release Updates and complete the security-related updates. You have {security.connectedApps|connected app|connected apps}: check in particular the migration to external client apps and the retirement of the username-password, user-agent, and device OAuth flows.
features.checkHint: Setup > Release Updates: check the enforcement date of each update.

explainer.what: Salesforce keeps tightening security rules, for example for logins, connections to other systems, and sending email. This page bundles all upcoming mandatory changes.
explainer.benefit: One overview of what to do by when, instead of scattered individual notes.
explainer.ifNothing: The changes are enforced on their dates anyway. Unprepared integrations or users may then stop working.

features.title: Delete a Migrated, Packaged External Client App
features.summary: An external client app migrated from a connected app can now be deleted even in Packaged state. Afterward, the original connected app becomes active again.
features.recommendation: If a migration from connected app to external client app went wrong, turn on Allow deletion of migrated packaged external client apps in Setup > External Client App Settings and delete the app. First make sure it isn't part of a released package.

explainer.what: Connections to other systems are currently being moved to a new format. If something went wrong, you can now delete the new version and the old one takes over again.
explainer.benefit: A safe way back if a migration causes problems.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Check Connected App Security Controls on the Insights Page
features.summary: The Insights page shows for all external client apps and connected apps whether security controls are missing, including disabled and externally developed apps. You can add missing controls directly or disable the app.
features.recommendation: You have {security.connectedApps|connected app|connected apps}. Open Setup > Insights, look for apps with missing controls in the Security Controls column, and turn them on for local apps via Manage App. For packaged apps, contact the developer or disable the app until it's updated.

recommendationVariants.text: You have {security.connectedApps|connected app|connected apps}, so a systematic review pays off. Open Setup > Insights, sort by missing security controls, and disable unused apps first. Add the controls to local apps via Manage App, and contact the developer for packaged apps.

explainer.what: Connected apps are how other programs connect to Salesforce, such as accounting software. A new overview shows which connections are missing recommended protection settings.
explainer.benefit: Weak spots in integrations become visible at a glance and can be fixed quickly.
explainer.ifNothing: Insecurely configured connections stay unnoticed.

features.title: Suspicious API Access Can Trigger Reauthentication or Freezing
features.summary: If Salesforce detects suspicious API data-access behavior, it terminates sessions and emails admins; in extreme cases it freezes the user and revokes all access. Clarified: when this happens and how to resume afterward.
features.recommendation: Make sure admin email addresses are monitored so these alerts don't get lost. Check that your integrations log in again cleanly after a session ends, and decide who unfreezes users after review.

explainer.what: If an account suddenly pulls unusually large amounts of data through an interface, Salesforce steps in automatically: the session ends, in serious cases the account is frozen, and admins get an email.
explainer.benefit: Data theft through stolen access is stopped early.
explainer.ifNothing: The protection works anyway. Without preparation, though, an integration may stop unexpectedly until someone reacts.

features.title: Speed Up Custom Pages with the defer Attribute on Script Tags
features.summary: Because Salesforce renders Content Security Policy as a meta tag, Chrome downloads external scripts on custom pages (Visualforce, Apex pages, Lightning container components) one at a time. The defer attribute restores parallel downloads while keeping execution order.
features.recommendation: You have {dev.vfPages|custom Visualforce page|custom Visualforce pages}. Check which of them load external scripts and add defer="true" to those script tags. Then test that inline scripts depending on these libraries still work.

explainer.what: Older custom-coded pages in Salesforce currently load add-on scripts one after another in Chrome instead of at the same time. A small code change makes them load in parallel again.
explainer.benefit: Custom pages open noticeably faster.
explainer.ifNothing: Everything keeps working; affected pages just load slower than necessary.

features.title: Security Center Essentials: Response Log for Automated Containment
features.summary: The Response Log in Security Center Essentials records every completed automated containment action with action type, status, affected entity, and timestamps for detection and response.
features.recommendation: You have the Security Center add-on. Regularly check Security Landscape > Response Log on the dashboard to see which actions Salesforce took automatically, and follow up on unusual cases with the affected users. Requires the View Security Center Pages permission.

explainer.what: When Salesforce detects a threat, it often reacts on its own, for example with an extra login check. A log now shows each of these reactions with time and result.
explainer.benefit: You quickly see which incidents are resolved and where you still need to follow up.
explainer.ifNothing: The automated responses still happen; you just have less visibility.

features.title: Security Center: Response Log for Automated Containment
features.summary: The Response Log in Security Center shows each completed automated containment action with action type, status, target entity, and timestamps, so you can tell resolved threats from open items.
features.recommendation: You have the Security Center add-on. Add the Response Log (dashboard > Security Landscape > Response Log) to your regular security review and look into repeated actions for the same user or integration.

explainer.what: Salesforce automatically fends off some detected threats. The security cockpit now lists all these interventions with time and result.
explainer.benefit: A clear record of what happened, including for audits.
explainer.ifNothing: Protection still works; you just have less visibility.

features.title: Salesforce Add-On for Gmail: Manage Data and Users from Gmail (Beta)
features.summary: The Salesforce add-on for Gmail lets you add contacts, view and edit accounts, contacts, opportunities, and cases, and invite or deactivate users. Starter Suite and Pro Suite only, currently in the United States only.
features.recommendation: Only relevant for Starter Suite or Pro Suite orgs in the United States with Google Workspace: have your Google Workspace admin install the add-on from the Marketplace and test it with a few users. Note that users can also be invited and deactivated through the add-on.
features.checkHint: Only available for Starter Suite and Pro Suite in the United States.

explainer.what: If you work a lot in Gmail, you can see and change customer data from Salesforce right next to the email without switching apps.
explainer.benefit: Less jumping between email and CRM.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. This is an optional beta feature.

features.title: Starter and Pro Suite: Draft Marketing Emails with the Email Authoring Agent
features.summary: In Starter Suite and Pro Suite, the Email Authoring Agent uses generative AI to turn a description into an email draft with a recommended layout. You refine tone and content in conversation or by hand.
features.recommendation: If you use Starter Suite or Pro Suite for marketing emails, turn on AI capabilities via the Agentforce icon (Agree and Enable) and try the agent for your next campaign (Marketing app > Content > CMS Workspace > Add > Email).
features.checkHint: Only available for Starter Suite and Pro Suite.

explainer.what: You briefly describe what a newsletter should be about, for example an invitation to an open house, and an AI creates a finished, designed draft.
explainer.benefit: Marketing emails in minutes instead of hours.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. You can still write emails by hand.

features.title: Salesforce Suites: New Learning Content in the Getting Started Tab
features.summary: The Getting Started tab adds the Close Your First Deal guided workflow (Free, Starter, Pro Suite) and the Meet Agentforce Coworker video (Starter, Pro Suite).
features.recommendation: If you're new to a Salesforce suite, point new users to the Getting Started tab in the Home app, especially the Close Your First Deal workflow.
features.checkHint: Only available for Free Suite, Starter Suite, and Pro Suite.

explainer.what: Companies just starting with Salesforce get new step-by-step guides, for example how to take a deal all the way to closing.
explainer.benefit: New users find their way around faster.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Agentforce Coworker in Starter Suite and Pro Suite
features.summary: Agentforce Coworker has been generally available and on by default for new Starter Suite and Pro Suite customers since October 20, 2026; existing customers follow in coming months. Third-party data ingestion and Coworker Skills aren't supported.
features.recommendation: If you use Starter Suite or Pro Suite, check whether Coworker is already active (Ask button next to search). Tell users what the assistant can do. If you don't want it, assign yourself the Agentforce Coworker Admin permission set and switch off the Agent Actions toggle in Advanced Setup.
features.checkHint: Only for Starter Suite and Pro Suite.

explainer.what: Customers on the smaller Salesforce packages get an AI assistant that answers questions about customers and deals and gets tasks done. For new customers it's on right away.
explainer.benefit: Faster answers and fewer clicks day to day; existing permissions still apply.
explainer.ifNothing: In new orgs the assistant is active automatically. If you don't want it, you have to switch it off yourself.

features.title: Starter and Pro Suite: Marketing App Provisioned Automatically
features.summary: New Starter Suite and Pro Suite orgs get the Marketing app with People Scoring, Tableau Next engagement reports, and a landing page site automatically. Older orgs have to turn on marketing features manually.
features.recommendation: If your Starter Suite or Pro Suite org was created before late October 2026 and you want to use marketing, open Advanced Setup > Marketing Features and click Turn On. New orgs don't need to do anything.
features.checkHint: Only for Starter Suite and Pro Suite.

explainer.what: The marketing tools in the smaller Salesforce packages are now ready immediately for new customers instead of after a wait and manual setup.
explainer.benefit: You can start marketing campaigns on day one.
explainer.ifNothing: In older orgs, marketing features stay off until someone turns them on.

features.title: Apromore: Process Insights with AI Recommendations Generally Available
features.summary: Apromore maps how business processes actually run, including variants and bottlenecks. New: data pipelines from Salesforce sources, KPI dashboards, AI improvement recommendations and simulations.
features.recommendation: Apromore needs its own license (Apromore Admin permission set license). If you want to measurably improve processes such as lead-to-order or case handling, ask for a demo and check whether your data (Salesforce objects, Data 360) is enough for a pipeline.

explainer.what: Apromore is a process mining tool: it analyzes which paths a process really takes, e.g. how long an order takes from inquiry to invoice and where it gets stuck.
explainer.benefit: You see bottlenecks based on real data instead of gut feeling and can simulate changes before rolling them out.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. It is an add-on product that is only used with a license.

features.title: Data 360: New Left-Side Navigation
features.summary: Data 360 gets a left-side navigation that groups related features, plus resource pages with enablement material. Existing customers turn it on or off in Feature Manager.
features.recommendation: In Data Cloud Setup > Feature Manager, enable "Data 360 Left Side Navigation" and test it with your Data 360 users. Users who customized their navigation or pinned tabs must reset it via the pencil icon with "Reset Navigation to Default".

explainer.what: Data 360 (formerly Data Cloud) had a lot of tabs. The new menu on the left groups them by topic, like a tidy table of contents.
explainer.benefit: Users find features faster and have help material at hand.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The current navigation stays until you switch.

features.title: Send Conversion Events from Data 360 via the OpenAI Conversion API
features.summary: Data 360 sends conversion events such as web purchases, event registrations or closed opportunities directly to OpenAI (Conversion API) to measure ad performance there. Requires an Ad Audiences license.
features.recommendation: Only relevant if you have an Ad Audiences license and advertise on OpenAI. Then create an OpenAI activation target in Data 360 and activate the relevant DMOs. Clarify with data protection first which events may be shared.
features.checkHint: Requires an Ad Audiences license. Check in Setup > Company Information.

explainer.what: Advertisers want to know whether ads lead to purchases. Data 360 can now report such successes (e.g. "customer bought") directly to OpenAI's ad platform.
explainer.benefit: You measure ad success more completely, even when browsers block tracking, and also for offline deals.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Without ads on OpenAI it doesn't matter.

features.title: Share Data 360 Objects with Microsoft OneLake (Beta)
features.summary: Zero-copy sharing: Data 360 objects can be queried in Microsoft OneLake as tables without copying the data. During beta, views and Salesforce filters aren't supported, so all rows are visible.
features.recommendation: If you use Microsoft Fabric/OneLake, test the beta in a non-production environment: Data Cloud Setup > Feature Manager > "Data Share for OneLake (Beta)". Note that all rows are shared and check beforehand which objects that affects.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you use Microsoft Fabric or OneLake.

explainer.what: Many companies run their analytics in Microsoft tools. Data 360 can make customer data visible there without creating a copy, like a window instead of a move.
explainer.benefit: No duplicate data storage, less interface maintenance, analytics on current data.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. It is an optional beta feature.

features.title: Share Data 360 Objects with Google BigQuery in Any Region
features.summary: Zero-copy sharing from Data 360 to Google BigQuery now works across regions: BigQuery can be in any region.
features.recommendation: If you use BigQuery and sharing failed so far because of the region, evaluate a data share connection now. Check whether cross-region data flows fit your data protection and data residency rules.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you use Google BigQuery.

explainer.what: Google BigQuery is a cloud data warehouse. Data 360 could only share data there if both were in matching regions. That restriction is gone.
explainer.benefit: More architectural freedom, no detours via copies.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Data Processing Engine: Control Currency Conversion
features.summary: In orgs with multiple currencies, you decide whether DPE definitions convert amounts to one currency or keep them in the original currency. Previously, the CRM Analytics and Data 360 runtimes behaved differently.
features.recommendation: If you use DPE definitions with currency fields, check which behavior your calculations expect. In the DPE builder under Set Up, turn "Currency Conversion" on or off deliberately and compare the results in a sandbox first.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with Data Processing Engine and multiple currencies enabled (Setup > Company Information).

explainer.what: The Data Processing Engine calculates large amounts of data in the background, e.g. totals per customer. With amounts in euros and francs, it wasn't consistent whether they were converted.
explainer.benefit: Consistent, traceable results no matter which platform runs the calculation.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing changes automatically. The differences between the runtimes remain.

features.title: Batch Data Transforms: Actions Directly in the Builder
features.summary: The Batch Data Transform builder now has Alerts, Search, Definitions, Settings, Run and Schedule in its header. Alerts and search results open next to the graph.
features.recommendation: No action needed. Let your Data 360 builders know that run, schedule and settings (including currency) are now directly in the builder.

explainer.what: Batch Data Transforms prepare data in Data 360, e.g. merging and cleaning. The most important buttons are now directly in the editing window.
explainer.benefit: Less jumping back and forth while building and troubleshooting.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. It is a usability improvement.

features.title: Deploy One Packaged Transform Across Multiple Connections
features.summary: A transform packaged in a data kit can be installed against a chosen connection; each copy is managed separately. Previously it pointed to fixed data lake objects and had to be rebuilt for additional connections.
features.recommendation: If you distribute transforms via data kits between orgs or for several data sources, review your kits: at install you now choose input and output DLOs per connection. Replace manually rebuilt transform copies step by step.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you use data kits with transforms.

explainer.what: A transform is a recipe that prepares data. Previously a prebuilt recipe only fit one specific data source. Now it can be reused for several sources.
explainer.benefit: Less rebuilding and easier maintenance when several systems need the same logic.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing transforms keep running.

features.title: Retriever Playground: Measure Context Precision for RAG
features.summary: In the Retriever Playground's advanced mode, Data 360 uses a test question and reference answer to compute a context precision score: it shows whether relevant chunks rank at the top of the result.
features.recommendation: If your agents retrieve knowledge through retrievers, create a few test questions with reference answers per retriever and measure the score in advanced mode. Note the billing considerations for testing retrievers (credit consumption).

explainer.what: Agents often answer questions with content from your documents (RAG). A retriever looks up the matching passages. The new score shows whether it returns the right passages first.
explainer.benefit: You can measure your agents' answer quality objectively and improve it in a targeted way.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. You just miss out on a metric.

features.title: Profile Engagements Widget Retiring: Move to the Engagement Timeline
features.summary: The Data Cloud Profile Engagements widget has reached end of life. Its replacement is the Data 360 Engagement Timeline for Account, Contact, Lead, Person Account and Prospect, with up to 10 engagement types.
features.recommendation: In Lightning App Builder, check which record pages still contain the Profile Engagements widget and replace it with the Data 360 Engagement Timeline. Configure the engagement types and test visibility with a regular user.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if the Profile Engagements widget is used on record pages (Lightning App Builder).

explainer.what: On customer or contact pages, a component showed how the person interacted with you, e.g. opened emails or visited the website. That component is being retired and replaced by a new timeline.
explainer.benefit: The new timeline shows more kinds of interactions clearly in chronological order.
explainer.ifNothing: The old widget is no longer developed and will eventually go away; sales and service then no longer see the interactions.

features.title: Data 360 Engagement Timeline on Record Pages
features.summary: A new widget shows Data 360 engagement data chronologically on Account, Contact, Lead and Person Account. Admins configure it in Lightning App Builder; users need a Data 360 license and object access.
features.recommendation: Add the Engagement Timeline to your key record pages, choose the relevant engagement objects and check permissions: users need a Data 360 license, access to the data space and explicit object permissions (control by parent isn't supported).

explainer.what: A timeline on the customer page shows what the person did recently: opened a newsletter, visited the website, made a purchase.
explainer.benefit: Sales and service see the customer's current interest at a glance and can respond better.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The data just stays invisible on the record page.

features.title: Copy Field Enrichments: More Field Types Compatible
features.summary: Copy Field Enrichments now maps between different field types, e.g. number to text or integer to percent; standard API casting handles the conversion. Empty source values clear the target field.
features.recommendation: Review existing copy field enrichments: helper formula fields created only for type conversion can be replaced by direct mapping. Watch target field lengths and note that empty source values now clear the target field instead of applying its default value.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you use Copy Field Enrichments.

explainer.what: Data 360 can copy values (e.g. a calculated customer score) into regular Salesforce fields. Previously the source and target field had to be exactly the same type; now, for example, number to text works.
explainer.benefit: Fewer helper fields and workarounds, simpler setup.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing mappings keep working, helper fields stay necessary.

features.title: Copy Field Enrichments: Write Values to Picklist Fields
features.summary: Copy field enrichments can now map source fields to picklist target fields, including dependent picklists.
features.recommendation: If you currently move Data 360 values into picklists via text fields and flows, consider a direct mapping to the picklist field. Make sure the source values match the allowed picklist values.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you use Copy Field Enrichments.

explainer.what: Picklists are fields with fixed values, e.g. "Industry". Data 360 can now fill such fields directly.
explainer.benefit: Fewer intermediate steps and cleaner data in Salesforce.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Build and Test Data 360 in Scratch Orgs
features.summary: Data 360 configurations can be built and tested alongside CRM metadata in scratch orgs. Usage costs fewer credits than in production and appears in Digital Wallet. Not in Government Cloud.
features.recommendation: If you develop Data 360 with source control, enable Data 360 for scratch orgs in production, check Dev Hub and add the CustomerDataPlatform feature to the scratch org definition. Scratch orgs with Data 360 expire after 7 days by default.

explainer.what: Scratch orgs are short-lived test environments for developers. Now you can try out Data 360 in them instead of building directly in a real environment.
explainer.benefit: Safer development, cleaner deployments and lower cost than testing in production.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Data 360 changes continue to be developed in sandboxes or production.

features.title: Agentic Content Email: Use Hosted CMS Images via URL
features.summary: When authoring email agentic content, you copy the URL of a published Salesforce CMS image into custom HTML. With image refresh enabled, later sends use updated images without republishing.
features.recommendation: If your marketers build agentic content emails with custom HTML, show them the CMS image URL approach and enable image refresh so image changes (e.g. seasonal visuals) apply without republishing.
features.checkHint: Applies to Marketing Cloud Next, Account Engagement or Engagement+ with the Salesforce Foundations add-on. Check your licenses in Setup > Company Information.

explainer.what: Marketing emails contain images. Now you can embed a centrally stored image by link; replace it centrally and future emails automatically show the new image.
explainer.benefit: Less rework when images change and consistent images across all emails.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Images are embedded as before.

features.title: Agentic Emails as HTML, Plain-Text or Text-Only
features.summary: Agentic content can now generate text-only emails. By default, emails include an HTML and a plain-text version; the text version can stay in sync or be customized separately.
features.recommendation: Check whether you have audiences that can't receive HTML (e.g. certain corporate mailboxes) and use text-only delivery for them. For everyone else, keep the plain-text version in sync so it stays current.
features.checkHint: Applies to Marketing Cloud Next, Account Engagement or Engagement+ with the Salesforce Foundations add-on. Check your licenses in Setup > Company Information.

explainer.what: Some recipients can't display designed emails. AI-assisted email creation now also produces plain text emails on request.
explainer.benefit: Better deliverability and readability for all recipients.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Emails keep going out as HTML with a text version.

features.title: Test Marketing Object Changes in a Sandbox and Sync with Data 360
features.summary: Marketing object schema changes can be tested in sandboxes and deployed via change sets; schemas replicate on sandbox refresh. Starting mid-November 2026, marketing objects sync with Data 360.
features.recommendation: From now on, change marketing objects in a sandbox first and deploy via change set; the deployer needs the Manage Marketing Objects permission. Then decide which marketing objects to sync with Data 360 for use in messages and flows.
features.checkHint: Applies to Marketing Cloud Next Advanced, Account Engagement Plus/Advanced/Premium or Engagement+ Corporate/Enterprise/Enterprise Plus with Salesforce Foundations.

explainer.what: Marketing objects store your own marketing data, e.g. event registrations. Changes to them can now be tried out safely in a test environment first.
explainer.benefit: Less risk when changing things, and data directly usable for personalized messages.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Changes keep happening directly in production, with the associated risk.

features.title: Build Personalization Once and Reuse It Across Every Channel
features.summary: Data sources, expressions and dynamic content blocks are created once and reused in SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, push and in-app. Starting mid-November 2026, Marketing Cloud appends UTM parameters to tracked links automatically.
features.recommendation: Collect your key personalizations (salutation, offers, data fields) as reusable expressions and dynamic blocks in the Data Sources tab instead of rebuilding them per channel. Also define central UTM parameters once.
features.checkHint: Applies to Marketing Cloud Next, Account Engagement or Engagement+ with the Salesforce Foundations add-on. Check your licenses in Setup > Company Information.

explainer.what: Personalization means e.g. "Hi Anna, your offer: ...". Previously you had to set it up separately for each channel (SMS, WhatsApp, push). Now you build it once and use it everywhere.
explainer.benefit: Less maintenance and the same messaging for the same customer across all channels.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Personalization stays duplicated per channel.

features.title: Simplify Marketing Trigger Setup and Save Data 360 Credits
features.summary: Marketing triggers now only require the mandatory DMO fields to be mapped. For the Abandoned Shopping Cart trigger, you choose whether to keep tracking cart state after flow entry.
features.recommendation: If you use retail triggers, review your mappings: map optional DMO fields only if you need them for personalization. For the abandoned cart trigger, decide deliberately whether cart state tracking is worth the extra Data 360 credits.

explainer.what: Triggers start messages automatically, e.g. a reminder when someone doesn't complete their cart. Setup is now simpler, and you can turn off costly extra tracking.
explainer.benefit: Faster setup and lower data processing costs.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Triggers run as before, possibly with unnecessary credit consumption.

features.title: Send Time Attributes: Store Values at Send Time
features.summary: Custom values such as coupon codes or flight numbers are stored with the send event at send time and can be used as report filters, segment criteria or export fields. The message itself isn't stored.
features.recommendation: Agree with marketing which values must be traceable for reports and audits (e.g. coupon code per recipient). Turn on send time attributes, define those attributes and have marketers map them in campaigns and flow messages.

explainer.what: When an email contains a personal coupon code, it was hard to trace later who got which code. Now that value is stored with the send.
explainer.benefit: Traceability for audits and customer inquiries, plus better reporting.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Send values stay only in the message and are hard to analyze later.

features.title: B2B Analytics for Marketers: Ready-to-Use Marketing Impact Dashboards
features.summary: B2B Analytics for Marketers brings account, opportunity, campaign, engagement and attribution data into Tableau Next dashboards. Advanced editions only, not Growth.
features.recommendation: If you have Advanced editions and want to prove marketing's pipeline contribution, set up B2B Analytics for Marketers in Setup from Marketing Cloud Assistant Home. Check first that campaigns are properly linked to opportunities, otherwise the dashboards stay empty.
features.checkHint: Only with Marketing Cloud Next Advanced, Account Engagement Plus/Advanced/Premium or Engagement+ Corporate/Enterprise/Enterprise Plus with Salesforce Foundations.

explainer.what: Marketing often has to prove which campaigns lead to revenue. Ready-made dashboards now show this based on campaigns, opportunities and customer interactions.
explainer.benefit: Informed budget and planning decisions without a custom reporting project.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Analysis stays manual work.

features.title: Recommenders Pick the Best Image per Recipient
features.summary: ML-based recommenders choose, at send time, the best image for each email recipient from a pool you define, based on profile and engagement history, and learn from opens and clicks.
features.recommendation: Test recommenders in a campaign with several image variants (e.g. product visuals) and compare click rates with a fixed image choice. Keep the image pool small and on-brand.
features.checkHint: Applies to Marketing Cloud Next, Account Engagement or Engagement+ with the Salesforce Foundations add-on. Check your licenses in Setup > Company Information.

explainer.what: Instead of showing every recipient the same image, the system picks the visual each person is most likely to respond to, e.g. hiking boots instead of sneakers.
explainer.benefit: Higher click rates without manual segmentation.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. All recipients keep seeing the same image.

features.title: Approved Attachments in Email Templates (Distributed Marketing)
features.summary: Starting November 2026, marketers can attach files to email templates and mark them as required. If enabled, Distributed Marketing senders can also upload their own files from a content workspace.
features.recommendation: If sales or advisors send templates via Distributed Marketing, attach required documents (e.g. terms, data sheets, legal notices) directly to the templates. Decide deliberately whether senders may attach their own files.
features.checkHint: Requires Data 360, Salesforce Foundations and the Distributed Marketing and Alerts (or Sales Emails and Alerts) add-on.

explainer.what: Field reps or advisors send marketing emails from central templates. Now important documents, such as product sheets or mandatory information, can be attached permanently.
explainer.benefit: Important documents are no longer forgotten and communication stays compliant.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Attachments keep being sent manually or not at all.

features.title: WhatsApp Account Model Update: One Number Across Providers
features.summary: Meta is separating business phone numbers from provider-specific templates and billing. One WhatsApp number can run with Salesforce and another provider at the same time. Meta migrates existing accounts automatically.
features.recommendation: With a single messaging account per number, no action is needed. If you share a number with another provider, note that opt-outs don't sync between providers. Use one provider where possible or record opt-outs manually in Salesforce.
features.checkHint: Only with the WhatsApp add-on. Relevant mainly if a number is also used with another provider.

explainer.what: Meta, the operator of WhatsApp, is changing how business numbers are managed. A number can now be used with several service providers at the same time.
explainer.benefit: More flexibility, e.g. marketing via Salesforce and customer service via another provider with the same number.
explainer.ifNothing: With only one provider, nothing. With a shared number, a customer who opts out with one provider can keep receiving messages from the other.

features.title: Republish Marketing Cloud Next Landing Pages (Release Update)
features.summary: Landing pages that haven't been published in a while can sit on outdated infrastructure and load more slowly. Republishing moves the content unchanged to the current infrastructure.
features.recommendation: In the Content Workspace for Marketing Cloud, open Settings > Publication Calendar and republish every landing page last published more than 6 months ago. Plan this as a recurring task.
features.checkHint: Check Setup > Release Updates and the Publication Calendar in the content workspace.

explainer.what: Landing pages are campaign web pages, e.g. a sign-up form. If you don't republish them for a long time, they keep running on old technology.
explainer.benefit: Faster, stable pages for your campaigns without any content change.
explainer.ifNothing: Old pages can get slower, which costs visitors and sign-ups.

features.title: Forms: Show or Hide Dependent Fields Based on Input
features.summary: In Form Builder, visibility rules show fields only when relevant, e.g. state after country. If an answer changes, dependent values are removed. Up to 50 rules per form, nested two levels deep.
features.recommendation: Check whether you maintain several nearly identical forms for regions or audiences and merge them into one form with visibility rules. Give each field a label and a unique name for this.
features.checkHint: Applies to Marketing Cloud Next, Account Engagement or Engagement+ with the Salesforce Foundations add-on. Check your licenses in Setup > Company Information.

explainer.what: A form shows the "State" field only after someone selects "United States" as the country. That keeps the form short and relevant.
explainer.benefit: Fewer forms to maintain and cleaner data, because no contradictory answers are submitted.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. You keep maintaining separate or longer forms.

features.title: Buyer Engagement Agent: Qualify Leads and Book Meetings with an Agent
features.summary: The Buyer Engagement agent handles inbound lead generation and outbound nurturing: personalized emails, web chat, lead qualification and meeting booking. Setup is now in Salesforce Go, including a data graph and the conversation data kit.
features.recommendation: If you have many marketing leads that sales doesn't follow up on promptly, evaluate the agent: Salesforce Go > Buyer Engagement > Set Up. Start with one channel and clear qualification criteria agreed with sales.
features.checkHint: Applies to Marketing Cloud Next Advanced, Account Engagement Plus/Advanced/Premium or Engagement+ Corporate/Enterprise/Enterprise Plus with Salesforce Foundations. Not in Government Cloud.

explainer.what: An AI agent answers prospects by email or chat, asks follow-up questions, checks whether there is real buying interest and books a meeting with sales directly.
explainer.benefit: No lead is left waiting, and sales gets prequalified meetings.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Leads keep being followed up manually.

features.title: RCS Messaging: Carousels, Campaign Tab, More Countries and Conversational Billing
features.summary: RCS gets carousels with up to 10 cards, location and calendar buttons, business unit assignment, management in the Campaign tab, flow metrics, more countries (incl. Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Poland) and conversational billing outside the US.
features.recommendation: If you use or plan the RCS add-on, check the new countries for your target markets and conversational billing (messages within 24 hours count as one conversation). Manage RCS campaigns in the Campaign tab from now on.
features.checkHint: Requires the RCS add-on and Salesforce Foundations.

explainer.what: RCS is the successor to SMS, with images, buttons and carousels right in the phone's messaging app. Salesforce is expanding its features and countries.
explainer.benefit: More engaging mobile messages in more markets and more predictable costs.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Without the RCS add-on it has no effect.

features.title: Reuse Agentic Content Blocks in Email, SMS, MMS and RCS
features.summary: A multi-channel agentic content block is created once and added to email, SMS, MMS and RCS. Changes to the parent block update automatically in all messages that use it.
features.recommendation: Identify content you repeat across channels (footers, legal notices, offer modules) and create reusable agentic content blocks for it. Before editing a parent block, check which messages use it.
features.checkHint: Applies to Marketing Cloud Next, Account Engagement or Engagement+ with the Salesforce Foundations add-on. Check your licenses in Setup > Company Information.

explainer.what: A text module, e.g. a discount notice, is created once and used in emails and mobile messages. Change it and it changes everywhere.
explainer.benefit: Less duplicate maintenance and no outdated text in individual channels.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Modules keep being maintained per channel.

features.title: Marketing Planning and Operations Agent: Turn Strategy into Plans
features.summary: An agent builds connected marketing programs and goals along your planning hierarchy, cascading from leadership to teams or standalone for specific objectives. Requires the Agentforce for Marketing add-on.
features.recommendation: If you license Agentforce for Marketing, test the agent with a real planning cycle (e.g. quarterly planning). Set up your planning hierarchy first so the agent assigns programs and goals correctly.
features.checkHint: Requires the Agentforce for Marketing add-on plus Marketing Cloud Next Advanced, Account Engagement Plus/Advanced/Premium or Engagement+ Corporate/Enterprise/Enterprise Plus with Salesforce Foundations.

explainer.what: An AI assistant helps turn the marketing strategy into concrete programs and measurable goals for the teams instead of maintaining them in spreadsheets.
explainer.benefit: Less planning effort and more time for strategy and creative work.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Planning stays manual work.

features.title: Set Up Marketing Planning and Operations from Salesforce Go
features.summary: Salesforce Go brings setup and usage tracking for Marketing Planning and Operations together in one place in Setup, with help content. With the Your Account app turned on, some add-on licenses can be purchased directly.
features.recommendation: If you roll out Marketing Planning and Operations, start in Setup > Salesforce Go, filter by Marketing Cloud Next and follow the guided setup.
features.checkHint: Requires the Agentforce for Marketing add-on plus Marketing Cloud Next Advanced, Account Engagement Plus/Advanced/Premium or Engagement+ Corporate/Enterprise/Enterprise Plus with Salesforce Foundations.

explainer.what: Salesforce Go is a central setup page. Marketing planning, including guidance, can now be found there too.
explainer.benefit: Faster, guided setup.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Goal-Driven Marketing Programs with Planning Hierarchies
features.summary: Planning hierarchies can be tailored to each part of the marketing organization. Programs at different levels get goals whose results roll up automatically through the hierarchy.
features.recommendation: First model your marketing organization as a planning hierarchy (e.g. region > team) and define a few measurable program goals per level. Keep the hierarchy lean, otherwise roll-ups get confusing.
features.checkHint: Requires the Agentforce for Marketing add-on plus Marketing Cloud Next Advanced, Account Engagement Plus/Advanced/Premium or Engagement+ Corporate/Enterprise/Enterprise Plus with Salesforce Foundations.

explainer.what: The marketing strategy is broken down into programs and goals per team, e.g. "500 new leads in region South". Results add up automatically to the overall view.
explainer.benefit: Everyone sees how their work contributes to the strategy, and leadership sees overall progress.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Planning and goal tracking stay outside Salesforce.

features.title: Connect Campaigns to Programs and Goals
features.summary: A dedicated Planning and Operations tab on the campaign connects it to its program. Campaign results cascade into program goals and show the contribution to strategy.
features.recommendation: Link running campaigns to the right programs as soon as the planning hierarchy is in place. Set a rule that new campaigns are always assigned to a program.
features.checkHint: Requires the Agentforce for Marketing add-on plus Marketing Cloud Next Advanced, Account Engagement Plus/Advanced/Premium or Engagement+ Corporate/Enterprise/Enterprise Plus with Salesforce Foundations.

explainer.what: Each campaign, e.g. a newsletter or a trade show, is assigned to a parent program. That shows what it contributes to the annual goal.
explainer.benefit: A clear link between day-to-day work and company goals.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Campaigns keep standing on their own.

features.title: Marketing Governance: Tactic Templates, Compliance Reviews and a Unified Calendar
features.summary: Tactics and tactic templates speed up execution, compliance reviews check brand, regulatory and policy standards before launch, and a calendar shows all programs and campaigns. Coordination via tasks, approvals and Slack.
features.recommendation: Save proven processes (e.g. webinar, product launch) as tactic templates and define which programs need a compliance review before launch. Use the calendar in planning meetings to spot overlaps early.
features.checkHint: Requires the Agentforce for Marketing add-on plus Marketing Cloud Next Advanced, Account Engagement Plus/Advanced/Premium or Engagement+ Corporate/Enterprise/Enterprise Plus with Salesforce Foundations.

explainer.what: Recurring marketing activities are saved as templates, checked against rules before launch and planned in a shared calendar.
explainer.benefit: Faster execution, fewer compliance issues and no double-booked activities.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Coordination and reviews keep running via email and spreadsheets.

features.title: Test Personalized Content as Any Recipient
features.summary: Preview and test now work for list, individual and campaign recipients in email, SMS, WhatsApp, mobile app and RCS, with sample values from an activation, event, record or Apex. The rendered JSON can be reviewed and edited.
features.recommendation: Add the extended preview to your approval checklist: test personalized messages with two or three typical recipients per channel before sending. The feature rolls out per channel in phases during October and November 2026.
features.checkHint: Applies to Marketing Cloud Next, Account Engagement or Engagement+ with the Salesforce Foundations add-on. Check your licenses in Setup > Company Information.

explainer.what: Before a personalized message goes out, you can now see for each channel how it looks for a specific recipient, e.g. with their name and offer.
explainer.benefit: Fewer embarrassing mistakes such as empty placeholders or wrong offers.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Errors may only be noticed by the customer.

features.title: Automatically Append UTM and Custom Link Parameters
features.summary: Standard UTM parameters and custom parameters apply to all links in a business unit, a content record or a single link, with fallback values. Configured in Marketing Setup > Web Tracking. Available November 2026.
features.recommendation: In Marketing Setup > Web Tracking, define your standard UTM values with fallbacks and agree on the naming convention with your web analytics team. For business units that differ, use Manage Link Parameters on the business unit record.
features.checkHint: Applies to Marketing Cloud Next, Account Engagement or Engagement+ with the Salesforce Foundations add-on. Check your licenses in Setup > Company Information.
