explainer.what: UTM parameters are additions to links that let tools such as Google Analytics recognize which campaign a visitor came from. They are now appended to all links automatically.
explainer.benefit: Reliable reporting on where website visitors come from, without manual work per link.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Links still have to be tagged one by one, and gaps in reporting remain.

features.title: Marketing Cloud Engagement Automatically Revokes Compromised Client Secrets
features.summary: If Salesforce detects specific threats to an API integration, e.g. a client secret in a public code repository, the installed package's secret is revoked automatically. Admins are notified. It can't be turned off.
features.recommendation: Make sure the admin email addresses in Marketing Cloud Engagement are current and someone reads the notifications. Document for each integration how to generate and store a new client secret so a revocation doesn't cause a long outage.
features.checkHint: Marketing Cloud Engagement runs on its own platform and can't be detected from the org.

explainer.what: Integrations sign in to Marketing Cloud with a secret key. If that key shows up publicly on the internet, for example, Salesforce now blocks it immediately.
explainer.benefit: Protects against data leaks through stolen credentials.
explainer.ifNothing: The feature is active automatically. Without preparation, an integration can fail after a revocation until a new key is in place.

features.title: Use Marketing Cloud Engagement Images in Marketing Cloud Next Content Builder
features.summary: Using DAM Connect, images from Marketing Cloud Engagement can be inserted directly in Marketing Cloud Next Content Builder without downloading. Images update when the source changes. Planned after December 18, 2026.
features.recommendation: If you run Engagement and Next side by side, plan to set up Engagement as a DAM Connect provider (Marketing Admin permission) and drop duplicate image storage. The feature is planned only after December 18, 2026.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if Marketing Cloud Engagement and Next are used side by side.

explainer.what: If you use two Salesforce marketing systems, you had to upload images twice. Now the new system accesses the images of the old one directly.
explainer.benefit: One image source, no outdated copies.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Images keep being transferred manually.

features.title: WhatsApp: Service and Utility Messages Are Now Charged
features.summary: Since October 1, 2026, Meta charges per message for service messages and utility messages within the customer service window. Salesforce updates its pricing on November 1, 2026; overage billing can apply above your entitlements.
features.recommendation: Check how many WhatsApp service and utility messages you send per month and compare that with your entitlements. Agree with marketing whether automated confirmations need to go via WhatsApp or should use cheaper channels.
features.checkHint: Only applies with the WhatsApp channel in Marketing Cloud Engagement or Marketing Cloud Next.

explainer.what: Certain WhatsApp messages, e.g. replies to customers or order confirmations, used to be free. Meta now charges for them, and Salesforce passes this on from November.
explainer.benefit: Checking early avoids surprises on the invoice.
explainer.ifNothing: Messages keep being delivered, but overage charges can apply above your entitlements.

features.title: Marketing Cloud Engagement: Use TLS 1.3, Older Cipher Suites Retired
features.summary: Since Summer '26, Marketing Cloud Engagement no longer supports some TLS cipher suites. TLS 1.3 with SHA-256 or SHA-384 cipher suites is recommended. Also: proxied SAP domains, maxFileAgeHours for imports, retirement of Emotional Tone Insights.
features.recommendation: Check with the owners of your integrations and middleware that API calls to Marketing Cloud Engagement use TLS 1.3 with SHA-256/SHA-384 cipher suites. For import jobs, the maxFileAgeHours parameter helps prevent stale files from being imported.
features.checkHint: Marketing Cloud Engagement runs on its own platform and can't be detected from the org.

explainer.what: TLS is the encryption systems use to talk to each other securely. Older variants are being switched off; integrations should use the current version 1.3.
explainer.benefit: Secure connections and no sudden interface failures.
explainer.ifNothing: Integrations with outdated encryption can no longer connect.

features.title: Marketing Intelligence: AI Budget Reallocation Recommendations (Beta)
features.summary: Budget Reallocation in Marketing Intelligence analyzes campaign performance and uses AI to recommend how to reallocate the daily budget. You choose a target metric and campaigns and apply the recommendations you want.
features.recommendation: If you use Marketing Intelligence, turn on the beta in Setup > Marketing Intelligence > Feature Manager > "Budget Reallocation (Beta)" and compare the recommendations with your own decisions before applying them.
features.checkHint: Requires Marketing Intelligence in Marketing Cloud Next.

explainer.what: Ad budget is spread across several campaigns. The AI suggests moving money from weak campaigns to strong ones.
explainer.benefit: More impact per dollar of ad budget.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. It is an optional beta feature.

features.title: Salesforce Personalization Learning Map
features.summary: A learning map in Salesforce Help collects Trailhead modules, videos, blogs, developer guides and help topics on Salesforce Personalization, from first steps to Agentforce use cases.
features.recommendation: Share the learning map with the team that rolls out or runs Personalization, as a structured starting point instead of scattered sources.
features.checkHint: Requires the Salesforce Personalization add-on; usually can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: A collection of learning material, ordered by step, for anyone who wants to learn Salesforce Personalization.
explainer.benefit: Faster onboarding without searching.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Personalization: Experiment and Attribution Analytics on Demand
features.summary: Experiment and attribution analytics can be refreshed directly from the record, up to once per hour. Previously, only the 24-hour schedule existed; scheduled runs stay unaffected.
features.recommendation: Tell your Personalization users about "Update Analytics Now" on experiment or attribution records. Wait at least 24 hours after starting an experiment before refreshing manually so results are reliable.
features.checkHint: Requires the Salesforce Personalization add-on; usually can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: When testing which version of a web page performs better, you had to wait a day for new numbers. Now it's hourly at the push of a button.
explainer.benefit: Faster decisions during running tests.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Numbers keep arriving once a day.

features.title: Objective-Based Account Recommendations for B2B Sales
features.summary: Objective-based recommenders now consider account attributes such as industry, revenue and account type together with real-time engagement and recommend products or offers for goals like upsell or cross-sell, also in self-service portals.
features.recommendation: If you use Personalization and sell B2B, configure an objective-based recommender for cross-sell or upsell on account profiles. Check the data quality of industry, revenue and account type first, as the recommendations rely on them.
features.checkHint: Requires the Salesforce Personalization add-on; usually can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: Sales gets suggestions for which product a business customer might need next, e.g. what similar customers in the same industry have already bought.
explainer.benefit: More add-on sales through relevant, data-driven suggestions.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Recommendations stay a matter of the sales reps' experience.

features.title: Personalization Campaigns: Recommendations & Offers Strategy and Mobile Channel
features.summary: Personalization campaigns offer the Recommendations & Offers strategy with custom rules or AI, plus the mobile channel to personalize app experiences.
features.recommendation: If you use Personalization campaigns and have your own app, evaluate the new mobile channel. For offers, test the Recommendations & Offers strategy with rules first before switching to AI-based selection.
features.checkHint: Requires the Salesforce Personalization add-on; usually can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: Personalized campaigns show each visitor relevant content. New: also in your own mobile app and with AI-based offer selection.
explainer.benefit: Consistently personalized experiences on website and app.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Express Checkout (Apple Pay, Google Pay) in the B2C Shopper Agent on SFRA
features.summary: The B2C Shopper Agent can offer express checkout payment methods such as Apple Pay and Google Pay in the chat and show the order confirmation right there.
features.recommendation: If you use the B2C Shopper Agent on an SFRA storefront and already have express checkout implemented: have your development partner build the integration via cartridge (see the B2C Commerce Developer Guide) and test successful, failed and canceled payments.
features.checkHint: B2C Commerce runs on its own platform (Business Manager). Whether you use it can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: An online shop assistant (chat) answers customer questions about products. Now the customer can pay with Apple Pay or Google Pay right in the chat, without switching to checkout first.
explainer.benefit: Fewer clicks between question and purchase, which can mean more completed orders.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The chat assistant keeps pointing to the regular checkout.

features.title: B2C Commerce: Link to Deployment Schedules Added
features.summary: The B2C Commerce release notes overview page now links to the release and deployment schedules page in Salesforce Help.
features.recommendation: Informational only. If you plan B2C Commerce releases, you can now reach the deployment dates from the release notes overview in Salesforce Help.
features.checkHint: B2C Commerce runs on its own platform (Business Manager). Whether you use it can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: Salesforce added a link on the B2C Commerce overview page to the calendar of when new versions roll out.
explainer.benefit: Makes it easier to plan dates for testing and sign-off.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Account Manager: Link to Deployment Schedules Added
features.summary: The B2C Commerce Account Manager release notes page now links to the deployment schedules. Current versions: Account Manager 3.13 (Sept 23, 2026) and 3.14 (Oct 21, 2026).
features.recommendation: Informational only. If you manage Account Manager (user administration for B2C Commerce), you can now find the deployment dates directly from the release notes page.
features.checkHint: B2C Commerce runs on its own platform (Business Manager). Whether you use it can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: Account Manager is the user and access administration for B2C Commerce. Salesforce added a link to the update calendar.
explainer.benefit: You see sooner when changes to access administration are coming.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Measure Shopper Agent Analytics with the Agentforce Commerce Client
features.summary: For SFRA storefronts, Reports & Dashboards show how many orders, what conversion and what order value the B2C Shopper Agent influences. The data comes from the plugin_commerce_client cartridge, which replaces plugin_shopper_agent.
features.recommendation: If you use the B2C Shopper Agent on SFRA: install or redeploy plugin_commerce_client version 1.3.0 or later and check whether the replaced plugin_shopper_agent cartridge is still in use. Then use the Agent Assistance filter under Reports & Dashboards in Business Manager.
features.checkHint: B2C Commerce runs on its own platform (Business Manager). Whether you use it can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: When a chat assistant advises shoppers in your online store, you want to know whether it actually drives revenue. Now there are metrics comparing orders with and without the assistant.
explainer.benefit: You can prove whether the chat assistant pays off instead of guessing.
explainer.ifNothing: You have no figures on the assistant's success. If the old cartridge is still running, you miss out on new features.

features.title: AI Suggestions for Synonym Rules in B2B Search
features.summary: Instead of creating synonym rules by hand, AI suggests synonyms based on real search queries and catalog data. Admins review, modify or approve them. Available by request; requires Agentforce Merchant Agent and Data Cloud.
features.recommendation: If your B2B store search often returns no results and you have Agentforce Merchant Agent and Data Cloud: request the feature from your Salesforce Account Executive and review the suggested synonyms before approving them.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with Agentforce Merchant Agent. This can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: Shoppers search with typos, abbreviations or industry jargon (e.g. "SS screw" instead of "stainless steel screw"). Until now, such synonyms had to be maintained by hand. Now AI suggests them based on real searches.
explainer.benefit: Fewer searches with no results; buyers find products faster.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Synonyms continue to be maintained by hand.

features.title: Order Status in the Shipment Tracker for Localized Stores
features.summary: The Shipment Tracker on the Order Details page now shows the order status even when Order Summary Status values are translated. Takes effect after you republish the store.
features.recommendation: If your B2B store is multilingual and data translation is turned on: republish the store in Experience Builder, testing in a sandbox first.
features.checkHint: Only relevant for B2B stores with data translation and translated status values.

explainer.what: Customers using the store in a language other than English, e.g. German, didn't see an order status in shipment tracking. This is fixed.
explainer.benefit: Customers in every language see where their order is and contact support less often.
explainer.ifNothing: Without republishing, the status stays empty for non-English customers.

features.title: Maintain Multiple Carts at the Same Time (Generally Available)
features.summary: Advanced cart management is generally available: B2B buyers can keep several independent carts, e.g. one per project, and name, rename or delete them. Rolling out gradually.
features.recommendation: If your B2B customers order for different projects or locations: In Experience Builder, add the Product Detail Purchase Options, Cart Menu, Cart Container and Cart Detail components to the Product, Cart, Checkout and My Profile pages, testing in a sandbox first.

explainer.what: A buyer orders for three construction sites. Instead of putting everything into one cart, they create one cart per site and submit them separately.
explainer.benefit: Clearer orders, fewer errors and less rework with large customers.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Customers keep working with a single cart.

features.title: Saved Carts: Split Shipments, Coupons and Gift Options
features.summary: In saved carts, B2B buyers can ship to multiple addresses, add gift wrapping and messages, and apply coupon codes without switching to the default cart.
features.recommendation: If you use or are introducing advanced cart management: In Experience Builder, add the Product Detail Purchase Options, Cart Menu, Cart Container and Cart Detail components to the Product, Cart, Checkout and My Profile pages and check that your coupon and shipping logic works with multiple carts.

explainer.what: A customer has one cart for each of two projects. Now they can apply separate coupons in each and split delivery across several addresses.
explainer.benefit: More flexibility for buyers, fewer detours through customer service.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. These options are then only available in the default cart.

features.title: Request Quotes and Check Out from Any Saved Cart
features.summary: B2B buyers can request a quote or check out from any saved cart. Previously, this was only possible from the default cart. Rolling out from October 20, 2026.
features.recommendation: If your B2B customers request quotes in the store: In Experience Builder, add the Product Detail Purchase Options, Cart Menu, Cart Container and Cart Detail components to the Product, Cart, Checkout and My Profile pages and test the quote process with multiple carts.

explainer.what: A buyer puts together several orders in parallel. For each one, they can now request a quote or check out directly, without switching carts first.
explainer.benefit: Fewer clicks and fewer abandoned carts.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Quotes and orders continue to go through the default cart only.

features.title: Sort Carts by Date
features.summary: B2B buyers can sort their cart list by created or modified date. The default cart and the four most recently modified carts appear at the top.
features.recommendation: Comes automatically with advanced cart management once the cart components (Cart Menu, Cart Container, Cart Detail) are on your store pages. Otherwise, nothing to do.

explainer.what: Buyers with many carts find the one they need faster because the list can be sorted by date.
explainer.benefit: A bit more overview for buyers with many carts.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Share Carts with Team Members (View, Edit, Check Out)
features.summary: B2B buyers can share carts with colleagues on the same account and grant view, edit or check-out access, e.g. for internal approvals. Rolling out from October 20, 2026.
features.recommendation: If several people at your B2B customers work on one order: turn on cart sharing in the store's Cart settings and define permissions, add the cart components plus Shared Cart Activity, and publish the store.

explainer.what: An assistant builds the cart, the department head reviews and checks out. Previously, that meant sharing login details; now you simply share the cart.
explainer.benefit: Internal approvals at the customer work without shared passwords or duplicate work.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Customers keep making do with screenshots, emails or shared logins.

features.title: Import and Export Carts with a CSV File
features.summary: B2B buyers can fill a cart with many line items by importing a CSV file and export it as CSV before checkout to review or share it outside the store.
features.recommendation: If your B2B customers place large orders: in Experience Builder, add the Cart Detail component to the cart page, add the Cart Exports page to the My Account navigation, and republish the store. Import and export run asynchronously.

explainer.what: A buyer keeps their order list in Excel. Instead of clicking 200 items one by one, they upload the file and instantly have a full cart.
explainer.benefit: Large orders are much faster and have fewer typos.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Customers keep adding items one by one or via quick order.

features.title: Checkout with Payment, Gift Card and Fraud Commerce Apps (Beta)
features.summary: For Storefront Next, Payment, Gift Cards and Fraud Commerce Apps work together in checkout: authorization, partial payment with a gift card, reversal on failure, and fraud checks before authorization. Beta.
features.recommendation: Only relevant if you use or plan Storefront Next. Beta: check with your implementation partner whether your payment and fraud providers are available as Commerce Apps, and test outside production first.
features.checkHint: B2C Commerce runs on its own platform (Business Manager). Whether you use it can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: Several services work together at the online checkout: payment, gift cards, fraud checks. These can now be plugged in as ready-made building blocks, e.g. redeem a gift card and pay the rest by credit card.
explainer.benefit: Less custom development, fewer abandoned purchases and fewer fees for fraudulent orders.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Your existing checkout stays as it is.

features.title: Keep Point of Sale Up to Date with Partial Syncs
features.summary: Instead of waiting for a full catalog sync, you can schedule a delta sync that sends only changes such as product data, prices and translations to the point of sale.
features.recommendation: If you use B2C Commerce with POS catalog unification: in Business Manager, go to Merchant Tools | Site Preferences | Point of Sale, and on the Products tab in the Delta Feed section, turn on Auto-Sync and set a schedule.
features.checkHint: B2C Commerce runs on its own platform (Business Manager). Whether you use it can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: A retailer changes a price online. Until now, the in-store register only showed it after the next full sync. Now just the changes are transferred regularly.
explainer.benefit: Same prices and product info online and in store, fewer problems at the register.
explainer.ifNothing: Register and online store can differ between two full syncs.

features.title: Loyalty: Subcurrencies with Mixed Expiration Models
features.summary: With the Activity With Mixed Subcurrencies expiration model, the parent currency expires based on activity while subtypes can expire on a fixed or activity basis. Now available to all customers with Loyalty Management Growth or Advanced, no longer by request only.
features.recommendation: If you use Loyalty Management Growth or Advanced and want to time-limit, for example, promotional or partner points: review your currency model and create new currencies with Activity With Mixed Subcurrencies. Optionally turn on traceability to link redemptions to accruals.

explainer.what: In a rewards program, regular points shouldn't expire as long as the member is active, but promotional points should expire after three months. This can now be set up within one points currency.
explainer.benefit: Better control of liabilities from outstanding points and more incentive to redeem promotional points promptly.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. All subcurrencies keep inheriting the parent currency's expiration model.

features.area: Salesforce Go Accelerators for Revenue Cloud
features.title: Automate Quote Approvals with Prebuilt Workflows
features.summary: Prebuilt workflows in Salesforce Go route quote discounts through approval levels based on thresholds, remind approvers of pending work and escalate overdue approvals. Requires Revenue Cloud Advanced.
features.recommendation: If you use Revenue Cloud Advanced and discount approvals slow down deals: in Salesforce Go under Quote Approvals, install the Quote Smart Approval and/or Approval Follow-Up and Auto-Escalation bundles in a sandbox, adjust thresholds to your discount policy and test.

explainer.what: A sales rep gives a 25% discount that the sales manager has to approve. If the approval sits idle, the system sends a reminder automatically and escalates to the next level after a deadline.
explainer.benefit: Approvals don't get stuck, deals close faster and discount rules are followed.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Approvals keep running as currently set up.

features.title: Billing: New Flow Action for Credit Memo Refunds
features.summary: The new processRefundCreditMemo invocable action processes refunds against posted credit memos and can be used in flows. Salesforce removed the earlier details on asynchronous billing schedule creation.
features.recommendation: If you use Revenue Cloud Billing and handle refunds on credit memos manually or with Apex: check whether the process can be built in a flow with the processRefundCreditMemo action.

explainer.what: When a customer gets a credit memo and should receive the money back, that was often manual work. Now there's a ready-made building block that automations can use to trigger the refund.
explainer.benefit: Refunds are faster and more consistent, with fewer manual booking steps.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Refunds keep running as before.

features.area: Salesforce Go Accelerators for Revenue Cloud
features.title: Revenue Cloud Accelerators: Prebuilt Building Blocks for Implementation
features.summary: New accelerators provide prebuilt foundations and sample data: autofill quotes from opportunity data, manage quote documents and DocuSign signatures, validate orders before activation, connect fulfillment to Field Service, and automate quote approvals.
features.recommendation: If you're implementing or extending Revenue Cloud: review the accelerators in Salesforce Go and check which ones can replace custom work (e.g. Quote Autofill, activation gate). Install them in a sandbox first.

explainer.what: Instead of building every process in Revenue Cloud yourself, there are now ready-made building blocks, e.g. "fill the quote automatically with data from the opportunity" or "only activate an order when all required details are correct".
explainer.benefit: Faster implementation, less project effort, less data entry for sales.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. You keep building yourself or with partners.

features.title: Automatically Reconcile Billing Schedules for Early Renewals
features.summary: When a contract with a future-dated order is renewed early, Billing automatically creates a negative billing schedule to prevent double billing and a new positive one for the renewal.
features.recommendation: If you use Revenue Cloud Advanced or Billing and correct early renewals manually today: test a renewal case in a sandbox and check the billing schedules that are created. Users need the Billing Admin permission set.

explainer.what: A customer renews their contract before the already planned renewal starts. Previously, they risked being billed twice and accounting had to correct it by hand. Now the system balances it out itself.
explainer.benefit: No double invoices, fewer manual corrections in accounting.
explainer.ifNothing: The system reconciles automatically. If you keep existing manual corrections, they could end up being applied twice.

features.title: Show Invoice Lines Grouped by Product
features.summary: The new Invoice Line Summary tab groups invoice lines hierarchically by product, including usage, overage and milestone charges, with filters and a totals bar. Requires Revenue Cloud Billing.
features.recommendation: If you use Revenue Cloud Billing: check whether the Invoice Line Summary tab appears on your invoice page; if not, add the component in Lightning App Builder. Users need Billing Admin or Billing Operations User.

explainer.what: An invoice with many individual items (base fee, usage, overage) is hard to read. Now you see all items for a product grouped together and can expand them.
explainer.benefit: Customer questions about invoices are answered faster.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Invoices keep being shown line by line.

features.title: Manage Saved Payment Methods in Aura Experience Sites
features.summary: The new Saved Payment Methods for Aura component lets customers add, view, delete and set default payment methods in Aura-based Experience Cloud sites. Requires Revenue Cloud Billing.
features.recommendation: If you use Revenue Cloud Billing with an Aura-based customer portal: add the component in Experience Builder, configure it and republish the site. Users need the Billing Experience Cloud User permission set.

explainer.what: Customers can store and change their credit card or other payment methods themselves in the customer portal, instead of calling support.
explainer.benefit: Faster payments, fewer support requests.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Payment methods keep being maintained some other way.

features.title: Clone Large Quotes and Orders
features.summary: Cloning large quotes and orders no longer hits a line-item ceiling. The Clone API runs asynchronously and shows progress, a completion alert and specific error messages. Requires Revenue Cloud Advanced.
features.recommendation: If you use Revenue Cloud Advanced with large quotes: turn on Clone Quotes and Orders under Setup > Revenue Settings and test cloning a large quote in a sandbox.

explainer.what: A sales rep wants to copy a quote with thousands of lines as a template. Previously, a limit stopped this. Now the copy runs in the background and the rep is notified when it's done.
explainer.benefit: Large quotes no longer have to be rebuilt by hand.
explainer.ifNothing: Large quotes and orders can still only be cloned with limitations.

features.title: Generate Quote Documents via CLM with Nested Product Groups
features.summary: CLM Document Generation shows groups, subgroups (up to 5 levels) and bundles in the quote document in the same structure as the quote, even with up to 15,000 lines and 1,000 bundles. Requires Revenue Cloud Advanced.
features.recommendation: If you use Revenue Cloud Advanced with grouped quotes: set up a quote document template, add the Generate Quote PDF via DocGen quick action to the quote layout and test how groups are shown (indentation, bullets, color).

explainer.what: A quote is organized by location and product group. The customer's PDF now shows exactly the same structure as the sales rep's screen.
explainer.benefit: Clearer quotes for customers, less rework on documents.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Quote documents keep being generated as before.

features.title: Stack Multiple Renewals on Termed Assets
features.summary: Termed assets can be renewed even when a future-dated renewal is already active. Each new renewal starts at the end date of the most recent one. Not for ramped, usage-based or derived pricing assets.
features.recommendation: If you use Revenue Cloud Growth or Advanced and customers renew early: let your renewal team know they no longer need to wait for the previous renewal to activate, and review existing manual workarounds.

explainer.what: A customer has already renewed their license for next year and now wants to lock in another year at today's price. Previously, that was only possible once the first renewal was active. Now it works right away.
explainer.benefit: Sales can close renewals immediately and lock in prices early, without workarounds.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. You just don't use the additional option.

features.title: Install the Revenue Cloud Reference Solution for Subscription Selling in a Sandbox
features.summary: From Salesforce Go, you can install the Subscription Selling Solution in an empty sandbox: Revenue Cloud foundations plus sample products, price books, quotes and orders. Sandboxes only; requires Revenue Cloud Advanced.
features.recommendation: If you're planning a Revenue Cloud implementation for subscription models: install the Subscription Selling Solution in an empty sandbox under Salesforce Go > Revenue Cloud (filter Get Started) and use it as a reference for your target design.

explainer.what: Instead of starting from scratch, you install a ready-made example for selling subscriptions in a test environment and can try out quotes and orders right away.
explainer.benefit: A fast start and a better basis for discussion in the implementation project.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing.

features.title: Convert Simple Products into Bundles
features.summary: Existing simple products can be turned into bundles by changing the product type. Previously, this required a new product record.
features.recommendation: If you use Revenue Cloud and created duplicate products just to sell them as bundles: consider simply switching the product type to bundle from now on. Test the effects on pricing and reports in a sandbox first.

explainer.what: A product used to be sold on its own and should now be offered as a package with accessories. Instead of creating a new product, you simply switch the existing one to "bundle".
explainer.benefit: Fewer duplicate products in the catalog, cleaner reports.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Bundles keep being created as new products.

features.title: Sales Methodology Criteria Suggestions Without a Flow
features.summary: A setting generates sales methodology criteria suggestions in a nightly job, with no flow of your own. It's faster, and suggestions only use data the opportunity owner can access. Staggered rollout from early November 2026.
features.recommendation: If you use Sales Methodology with Pipeline Management: deactivate the flow created from the Process Sales Methodology Criteria Suggestions template, then turn on the Turn On Methodology Criteria Suggestions step on the Sales Methodology setup page. The setting can't be turned on while the flow is active.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with Agentforce for Sales and Sales Methodology set up in Pipeline Management.

explainer.what: Sales methodologies such as MEDDICC require certain points to be clarified for each opportunity. Salesforce suggests which points are met based on conversation data. This now runs automatically overnight, without a self-built automation.
explainer.benefit: One less automation to maintain, faster suggestions, data protection through visibility rules.
explainer.ifNothing: The existing flow keeps running. You just keep maintaining it yourself.

features.title: Engagement Agents: Billing per Lead Worked
features.summary: Engagement agents now offer the Pay per Lead Worked pricing model: a flat number of Flex Credits per lead the agents work within 30 days, instead of billing per action. Available since September 1, 2026; requires the Agentforce Lead Nurturing add-on.
features.recommendation: If you use Engagement agents: look at consumption in Digital Wallet and compare in Engagement Setup under Choose your Pricing Model whether Pay per lead worked is cheaper. The choice applies to all Engagement agents and can be changed at any time.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with the Agentforce Lead Nurturing add-on.

recommendationVariants.text: You had {activity.leadsLast90d|new lead|new leads} in 90 days. If Engagement agents perform many actions per lead, Pay per lead worked is usually cheaper: check consumption in Digital Wallet and compare the pricing model in Engagement Setup.

explainer.what: AI agents contact prospects automatically and follow up. Until now, every single action cost money. Now you can choose a flat price per prospect handled instead.
explainer.benefit: More predictable costs; according to Salesforce, cheaper for most customers.
explainer.ifNothing: Billing stays per action, which can be more expensive depending on usage.

features.title: Momentum: Capture and Analyze Customer Conversations Automatically
features.summary: Momentum automatically captures meetings, emails and recorded customer conversations in Salesforce. Executive Briefs in Slack, Call Coaching, automatic field updates and Smart Clips build on this foundation.
features.recommendation: If your sales team holds many video calls: check with your Salesforce contact whether Momentum is licensed or worthwhile, and clarify recording and data protection questions (consent, works council) before rolling it out.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with a Momentum license. This can't be detected from the org.

explainer.what: Customer conversations are recorded and summarized automatically: what was discussed, what risks exist, what the next steps are. Managers get a summary in Slack.
explainer.benefit: Less note-taking and data entry for reps, better overview and more targeted coaching for managers.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Conversations keep being documented manually.

features.title: Set Email Address Verification per Authorized Domain
features.summary: For each authorized email domain, you can set whether address verification for sending is always required, only for changed addresses, or never. Previously, turning it off required Support. Email-to-Case routing addresses and Experience Cloud site senders always require verification.
features.recommendation: If a trusted integration (e.g. an HR system or SSO provisioning) manages your users' email addresses: check Require Address Verification to Send Email for each domain under Setup > Authorized Email Domains. With Never, only admins with Manage Users or Modify All Data can change email addresses.
features.checkHint: Setup > Authorized Email Domains. Only relevant if user email addresses are managed centrally.

explainer.what: Before someone can send emails from Salesforce, they have to confirm their address via a link. If your IT manages addresses centrally anyway, this step can now be skipped for your own domain.
explainer.benefit: New employees can send emails right away, fewer support requests.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Verification stays required as before.

features.title: Spiff Mobile App Supports Multi-Factor Authentication
features.summary: The Salesforce Spiff mobile app now supports MFA with an authenticator app. Previously, users couldn't sign in to the app when MFA was required. Not available with SSO.
features.recommendation: If you use Salesforce Spiff without SSO: turn on Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) under Settings > Security in the Spiff Admin menu and tell users in advance that they need an authenticator app.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if you use Salesforce Spiff (commission management). This can't be detected from the org.

explainer.what: Spiff calculates sales commissions. In the mobile app, sign-in now also works with a code from an authenticator app. Previously, sign-in failed when this was required.
explainer.benefit: Better protection of sensitive commission data, and MFA can be enforced for mobile users too.
explainer.ifNothing: Without MFA turned on, access stays protected by the password alone.

features.title: Host Activity Platform Data in Australia and New Zealand
features.summary: Activity Platform Hyperforce infrastructure (Einstein Activity Capture, Einstein Conversation Insights, Inbox, Sales Engagement) is available in the ANZ region since the week of October 12, 2026.
features.recommendation: Only relevant if your org is hosted in Australia or New Zealand or you need data residency there: check with Salesforce whether your email and calendar data can be moved to the ANZ region.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with data residency in Australia/New Zealand and use of Einstein Activity Capture, Inbox or Sales Engagement.

explainer.what: Emails and meetings that Salesforce captures automatically from Outlook or Gmail can now also be stored in Australia and New Zealand for customers there.
explainer.benefit: Easier compliance with local data protection requirements, faster syncing.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Nothing changes for orgs outside this region.

features.title: Unify Sales and Marketing Email Engagement in Data 360
features.summary: Email engagement data from Sales Engagement can be stored in Data 360 alongside marketing data for a complete view of email interactions. Rolling out gradually from mid-October 2026.
features.recommendation: If you use Sales Engagement and Data 360: go through Unify Email Engagement Data in the Track Performance and Success section under Setup > Sales Engagement Settings. Email syncing via Einstein Activity Capture is a prerequisite.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with Sales Engagement. This can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: A customer receives newsletters from marketing and personal emails from sales. Now you can see in one place which emails they opened or clicked, regardless of who sent them.
explainer.benefit: Sales and marketing see the same picture of the customer and coordinate contacts better.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The data stays separate.

features.title: Email Engagement Push Notifications in Salesforce and Outlook
features.summary: Sellers get browser push notifications when leads engage with sales emails, now also in Salesforce and in the Outlook extension. Previously, only in the Chrome extension.
features.recommendation: If you use Sales Engagement: let sellers know they can allow notifications for the Salesforce URL in their browser and turn on Show Notifications under My Feed (gear menu) in the Work Queue.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with Sales Engagement. This can't be reliably detected from the org.

explainer.what: When a prospect opens a sales email or clicks a link, the seller immediately gets a browser notification and can call promptly.
explainer.benefit: Sellers react faster to interest, regardless of the browser.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Notifications remain available only in the Chrome extension.

features.title: Forecasting Agent Supports the Forecasting Process
features.summary: Forecasting Agent analyzes pipeline changes, highlights deals that matter for hitting quota and helps complete forecast submissions. Requires Agentforce for Sales or Agentforce 1. Rolling out from October 19, 2026.
features.recommendation: If you use Collaborative Forecasts and Agentforce for Sales: turn on Forecasting Agent under Setup > Forecast Settings, pilot it with a few sales managers and compare its insights with your existing forecast call.
features.checkHint: Only relevant with Agentforce for Sales or Agentforce 1 and forecasts set up.

recommendationVariants.text: With {activity.opportunitiesLast90d|new opportunity|new opportunities} in 90 days, the agent can save a lot of time in forecasting: turn it on under Setup > Forecast Settings, pilot it with one sales team and compare its insights with your forecast call.

explainer.what: Sales managers regularly have to predict how much revenue will come in. An AI agent now shows which deals have changed, which are at risk and what's still missing to hit the target, and helps fill in the forecast.
explainer.benefit: More accurate revenue forecasts with less manual preparation.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Forecasts keep being prepared manually.

features.title: Offer Multiple Flow Approval Processes per Record
features.summary: The Request Approvals component lets submitters choose from up to 10 autolaunched flow approval processes, now also in Experience Builder.
features.recommendation: You have {automation.flowApprovals|flow approval process|flow approval processes}. Check whether an object has several approval paths side by side (for example discount and contract approval). If so, add the Request Approvals component to the record page, give each process a clear label, and decide whether comments and approver selection are allowed or required.

explainer.what: Approvals are sign-offs, for example "a discount above 20% needs the sales director's approval". If a record has several approval paths, users can now pick the right one from a list, also in a customer or partner portal.
explainer.benefit: Fewer questions about which approval path is the right one. Admins no longer need separate buttons or workarounds for each approval process.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing approvals keep running as before.

recommendationVariants.text: You have {automation.flowApprovals|flow approval process|flow approval processes} and a live Experience Cloud site. Besides the internal record page, consider adding the Request Approvals component to the object detail page in Experience Builder so partners or customers can start the right approval themselves.

features.title: Prevent Duplicate Email Sends in Marketing Flows
features.summary: Batch-based marketing flows check for duplicate contact points before each send: each email address gets only one message within a time frame you choose. Suppressed recipients are logged.
features.recommendation: If you use Marketing Cloud Next: deduplication is on by default for new flows but not for existing ones. Open your Audience, Broadcast and On-Demand flows, turn on "De-duplication Email Message Sends" on the start element, and set a suitable lookback window.

explainer.what: When several people share one email address, such as a couple or a shared inbox like info@, that address used to get the same marketing email several times. Now each address gets it only once.
explainer.benefit: Fewer annoyed recipients, fewer unsubscribes, and a cleaner send log.
explainer.ifNothing: Existing flows keep sending duplicates until you turn the option on.

features.title: Catch Over-Long Field Values When You Save a Flow
features.summary: If a Create or Update Records element sets a fixed text value longer than the target field allows, Flow Builder warns you on save. The flow still saves but fails at run time.
features.recommendation: You have {automation.activeFlows|active flow|active flows}. Watch for warnings in the validation panel the next time you save and fix them right away, because otherwise the flow fails for your users. The check covers fixed text values only, not variables.

explainer.what: Flows are automations that, for example, create records. If a text value is longer than the field allows, the automation stops. Salesforce now warns while you build the flow instead of when a user runs into the error.
explainer.benefit: Fewer error messages in daily work and less troubleshooting for admins.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. You just miss the early warning.

features.title: Omnistudio: External Site Users Can Query Only Allowlisted Objects
features.summary: Omnistudio for Managed Packages blocks SOQL/SOSL queries from guest and portal users via HandleData() and HandleDataCards() unless every object is on an allowlist. The allowlist is enforced by default and starts empty.
features.recommendation: If you use Omnistudio for Managed Packages on Experience Cloud (Aura) sites: check right away which Flexcards, Vlocity Cards or custom components on your sites load data via SOQL/SOSL, and add the required objects to the allowlist. While the list is empty, these components show external users no records. Then test as guest and portal users; permissions and sharing now apply in user mode.

explainer.what: Omnistudio provides building blocks for customer portals, such as cards showing contract or invoice data. For security reasons, portal visitors can now only query objects that the admin has explicitly allowed.
explainer.benefit: Protects your data from unintended access by portal visitors.
explainer.ifNothing: Affected portal components stop showing data until the objects are allowed.

features.checkHint: Check Setup > Installed Packages for Omnistudio for Managed Packages (Vlocity) and whether your Aura sites use Flexcards or Vlocity Cards.

features.title: MuleSoft for Flow: New Connectors for Workday, Google Drive, Paychex and More
features.summary: MuleSoft for Flow: Integration adds new third-party connectors: Elasticsearch, Google Drive, Paychex, and Workday Absence Management, Expenses, Organizations and Staffing.
features.recommendation: If you have the MuleSoft for Flow: Integration add-on: check whether existing integrations with Workday, Google Drive, Paychex or Elasticsearch (custom Apex, middleware) can be replaced by a no-code connector in Flow. Without the add-on, there's nothing to do.

explainer.what: Connectors are ready-made links to other systems, such as the HR system Workday. A Salesforce automation can exchange data through them without any programming.
explainer.benefit: Integrations can be built and maintained faster and without developers.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing integrations keep running.

features.checkHint: Check Setup > Company Information > Permission Set Licenses or Licenses for MuleSoft for Flow: Integration.

features.title: Approval Work Items Update Without a Page Refresh
features.summary: The Orchestration Work Guide component shows new approval work items with a New badge; items completed by someone else are disabled and marked Outdated instead of disappearing.
features.recommendation: You have {automation.flowApprovals|flow approval process|flow approval processes}. Nothing to configure. Briefly tell approvers about the new New and Outdated badges so they don't try to work on items that are already done.

explainer.what: People who approve requests see their open tasks on the record page. Until now they had to reload the page to see changes. Now new tasks appear right away, and tasks finished by colleagues are marked as outdated.
explainer.benefit: Less duplicate work and less confusion when several approvers are involved.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The improvement arrives automatically.

features.title: Orchestration Work Items Update Without a Page Refresh
features.summary: The Orchestration Work Guide component shows new orchestration work items with a New badge; items completed by someone else are disabled and marked Outdated.
features.recommendation: If you use Flow Orchestration: nothing to configure. Briefly tell the people working on these items about the New and Outdated badges.

explainer.what: Orchestrations split multi-step processes across different people, for example when onboarding a customer. The task list on the record page now updates by itself.
explainer.benefit: Users see right away what's new and what a colleague has already finished.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The improvement arrives automatically.

features.checkHint: Check Setup > Flows (filter by type Orchestrator) to see whether you have active orchestrations.

features.title: AI Relationship Research as a Subagent in Agentforce Conversations
features.summary: The AI Relationship Research subagent shows the key people and companies around an account or contact in an Agentforce conversation, explains the relationships and recommends whom to engage and how.
features.recommendation: If you have an AI Relationship Research license: in Agentforce Builder, add the AI Relationship Research Sub Agent to your employee agent via Add from Asset Library, test it in Preview, and assign users the AI Relationship Research User permission set.

explainer.what: Sales reps want to know who really decides at a customer and who they know there. The AI assistant now answers that directly in the chat, with reasons and a suggestion for the best way in.
explainer.benefit: Faster preparation for customer meetings without switching screens.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The feature simply stays unused.

features.checkHint: Check Setup > Company Information for an AI Relationship Research license.

features.title: Flow Builder Generates Element Labels Automatically
features.summary: Flow Builder generates element labels from the properties you configure and updates them as you build. Labels you edit manually are kept. No Agentforce license is required.
features.recommendation: You have {automation.activeFlows|active flow|active flows}. Nothing to turn on. If you have naming conventions for flow elements, check whether the generated labels fit them and adjust the convention if needed.

explainer.what: Every step in an automation needs a name, such as "Find open orders". Until now you had to type it yourself. Now Salesforce suggests a suitable name.
explainer.benefit: Automations get built faster and are easier for others to understand.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The feature is on automatically.

features.title: Field Service App: Hide Out-of-Stock Products on Products Consumed
features.summary: The Products Consumed tab in the Field Service app now has the Include Out of Stock toggle, just like the Inventory tab, to show or hide out-of-stock products.
features.recommendation: Nothing to configure. Point technicians to the new toggle; it's off by default, so out-of-stock products are hidden.

explainer.what: Technicians record in the app which materials they used at the customer's site. They can now hide products that are currently out of stock and scroll less.
explainer.benefit: Faster material entry on site.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The toggle is available automatically.

features.title: Scheduling Console: Filter the Gantt to a Single Crew
features.summary: Dispatchers can filter the Scheduling Console Gantt to the members of one crew, from the crew popover or a resource row, and remove the filter at any time.
features.recommendation: If your dispatchers work with crews in the Scheduling Console: point them to the new crew filter. Nothing to configure.

explainer.what: Dispatchers plan the jobs of technician teams (crews) on a timeline. They can now show just one team with a single click.
explainer.benefit: Clearer planning when many teams are out at the same time.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The feature is available automatically.

features.title: Scheduling Console Opens on Today
features.summary: When reopened, the Scheduling Console automatically shows today's date (the start of the week for longer horizons) and marks today with a blue circle. Refreshing keeps the current view.
features.recommendation: Nothing to configure. Dispatchers no longer have to navigate back to today manually.

explainer.what: The dispatchers' planning view now jumps to today when it opens instead of staying on the last date viewed.
explainer.benefit: Fewer clicks and fewer mix-ups when planning.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The improvement arrives automatically.

features.title: Holidays Visible in the Scheduling Console Gantt
features.summary: Holidays appear as non-working time on the Gantt. An indicator shows which territory's Operating Hours record the holiday comes from.
features.recommendation: Check that holidays are fully maintained in the Operating Hours of your service territories, especially across several countries or regions. They are now visible to all dispatchers.

explainer.what: Dispatchers now see directly in their planning view on which days a region has a public holiday, so they understand why nothing can be scheduled there.
explainer.benefit: Fewer scheduling mistakes across regions.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Missing holidays in your setup data will just be more noticeable now.

features.title: Scheduling Console: Color-Coded Appointment Indicators
features.summary: Custom color palettes highlight SLA risks, work types, customer tiers or vehicle types in the Gantt, appointment list and map. Palettes from the Classic Dispatch Console carry over; status colors are removed.
features.recommendation: If you use color palettes in the Classic Dispatch Console: they carry over automatically. Check that they work well in the Scheduling Console, create new ones if needed (for example for SLA risk), and tell dispatchers that appointment statuses are no longer colored there.

explainer.what: Dispatchers see at a glance, by color, which appointments are urgent or which customer type they belong to, without opening each appointment.
explainer.benefit: Urgent jobs stand out faster and dispatchers react faster.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Without custom palettes, the view stays as it was.

features.title: Enterprise Sales Management: Upload Location and MACD PDFs to a Quote
features.summary: PDFs with product locations or MACD requests (move, add, change, disconnect) can be uploaded to a quote. Intelligent Document Processing reads the rows and generates quote members and quote line items.
features.recommendation: If you use Enterprise Sales Management with the Intelligent Document Processing add-on: configure the Product Location and MACD document types in custom metadata (field mapping, validation, normalization, match rules), turn on Einstein Prompt Builder, and test with real customer PDFs.

explainer.what: Business customers often send long PDF lists of sites or change requests. Instead of retyping them, Salesforce reads the PDF and builds the quote lines from it.
explainer.benefit: Much faster quotes for large business customers and fewer typos.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Lists keep being transferred by hand.

features.title: Enterprise Sales Management: Mass Discounts on Very Large Quotes
features.summary: Mass discounts now work on quotes with up to 50,000 line items and more than 4,000 root items; processing runs in the background in smaller batches. Previously it failed at about 3,600 root items.
features.recommendation: If you use Enterprise Sales Management and mass discounts on large quotes used to fail: review and remove workarounds (splitting quotes, applying discounts in parts). Nothing to configure.

explainer.what: For large business customers, a quote often has thousands of lines. Applying a discount to all of them at once used to fail. Now it works even on very large quotes.
explainer.benefit: Fewer failures and less manual work on large quotes.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The improvement arrives automatically.

features.title: Enterprise Sales Management: Remove Promotions from Large Quotes Without Timeouts
features.summary: Removing a promotion now touches only the affected line items; large deletions move to the background automatically with a status display. Standard Cart APIs must be enabled.
features.recommendation: If you use Enterprise Sales Management: check that Standard Cart APIs are enabled, because the improvement only applies then. Point sales reps to the new background status display.

explainer.what: When a promotion was removed from a large quote, the application often froze. Now it runs in the background and sales reps can keep working.
explainer.benefit: Smoother work on large quotes.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Without Standard Cart APIs, the old behavior stays.

features.title: Enterprise Sales Management: Split a Quote into a New or Existing Quote
features.summary: Sales reps select line items or records on a quote and move them to a new or existing quote without recreating them.
features.recommendation: If you use Enterprise Sales Management: point sales reps to the new split function and check whether custom solutions for copying line items become unnecessary.

explainer.what: Sometimes part of a large quote needs to be negotiated separately, for example for another site. The lines can now simply be moved to another quote.
explainer.benefit: No more re-entering line items.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Splitting stays manual work.

features.title: Trade Promotion Management: Stable Attributes for Automated UI Tests
features.summary: TPM grids and the Trade Planning page now have stable, versioned HTML data attributes for grids, rows, columns, cells and promotion groups. Browser tests no longer have to rely on CSS classes or DOM structure.
features.recommendation: If you cover Trade Promotion Management with automated browser tests (for example Selenium or Playwright): gradually switch your selectors to the new automation attributes. Without UI test automation, there's nothing to do.

explainer.what: Some companies test their Salesforce screens automatically with scripts. For the planning tables for retail promotions, these tests often broke after updates. Now there are fixed markers the scripts can rely on.
explainer.benefit: Fewer broken tests after Salesforce releases.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing tests keep running but stay fragile.

features.title: Education Cloud: New Connect REST APIs for Student Financials
features.summary: New GET resources return a student's financial summary (charges, payments, outstanding balance), an itemized list of academic charges, and invoices with amounts and due dates.
features.recommendation: If you use Education Cloud with student financial data: check with your developers whether portals or integrations that assemble this data themselves can move to the new resources under /connect/education/student-financials.

explainer.what: Universities want to show students, for example in a portal, which fees are still open. There are now ready-made interfaces that deliver this data in one bundle.
explainer.benefit: Less custom development for financial overviews in portals and apps.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing solutions keep running.

features.title: Education Cloud: New Metadata Types for Delegating Access to Proxies
features.summary: The new metadata types DelegateAccessDef, DelegateAccessDataSet and DelegateAccsDataSetObj define which student data is shared with proxies (such as parents) and at which access level.
features.recommendation: If you want students to give parents or other proxies access: add the delegated access configuration via the new metadata types to your deployment process (sandbox to production).

explainer.what: Students can, for example, let their parents see grades or invoices. Which data that covers can now be moved as configuration between test and production systems.
explainer.benefit: Sharing settings can be tested and rolled out cleanly.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The types only matter for deployments.

features.title: Energy & Utilities: Retrieve and Summarize Energy Accounts with Agentforce
features.summary: New Agentforce actions return contacts with roles, account details, and a summary of service agreements, interactions, open cases and billing: Get Contacts by Account, Get Account Details, Account Summarization.
features.recommendation: If you use Agentforce for Energy & Utilities: add the three actions to your employee agent for sales and service and test them with typical customer questions. Note that the Employee Agent consumes Flex Credits.

explainer.what: A service rep at a utility asks the AI assistant "Summarize this customer for me" and gets contracts, recent contacts, open issues and billing status in one answer.
explainer.benefit: Faster call preparation and fewer clicks through many records.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The actions simply stay unused.

features.title: Energy & Utilities: Retrieve Billing Accounts and Premises with Agentforce
features.summary: New Agentforce actions show all billing accounts of an account (status, billing-system reference, relationship type) and the related premises with addresses: Get Billing Accounts for an Account, Fetch All Premises by Billing Account.
features.recommendation: If you use Agentforce for Energy & Utilities: add the actions to your employee agent, for example for move requests, and test them. The Employee Agent consumes Flex Credits.

explainer.what: When a customer calls about moving house, the rep sees all of the customer's billing accounts and addresses right away through the AI assistant.
explainer.benefit: Faster handling of moves and billing questions.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The actions simply stay unused.

features.title: Energy & Utilities: Retrieve Service Agreements and Meter Readings with Agentforce
features.summary: New Agentforce actions return energy service agreements per billing account and location, including agreement items and service points, and meter readings directly from the billing system.
features.recommendation: If you use Agentforce for Energy & Utilities: add the actions Fetch Energy Service Agreements by Billing Account and Location and Get Meter Readings From Billing System to your employee agent and test the billing-system connection. The Employee Agent consumes Flex Credits.

explainer.what: When a customer asks about their contract or latest meter reading, the AI assistant fetches the data directly, including from the billing system.
explainer.benefit: Shorter calls about contracts and consumption.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The actions simply stay unused.

features.title: Financial Services: Build Agents in the New Agentforce Builder
features.summary: The Agentforce Financial Services agents are available in the new Agentforce Builder, now also with the Banking Service Customer Assistance and Banking Service Employee Assistance templates. Existing agents are not affected.
features.recommendation: If you use Agentforce for Financial Services: create new agents in the new builder from one of the Financial Services templates. Upgrade existing agents in a sandbox and test them before migrating them in production. Switching is not mandatory.

explainer.what: Banks and insurers build AI assistants for customers and employees. There's now a new guided tool with ready-made templates, for example for loan requests or complaints.
explainer.benefit: Agents can be built and tested faster, and problems are easier to find.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing agents keep running.

features.title: Financial Services: Manage Household Relationships with Prebuilt Flows
features.summary: The new Household Management Graph (also for Managed Package) launches prebuilt flows with validation for actions such as adding a member instead of standard record pages, replacing the legacy household graphs.
features.recommendation: If you use households in the Actionable Relationship Center: test the prebuilt flows in a sandbox, clone and adapt them to your rules if needed, and then assign them to the node actions of the Household Management Graph in the Actionable Relationship Center.

explainer.what: Advisors maintain who belongs to a client household, such as spouses and children. Instead of an empty form, a guided assistant now walks through the entry and checks the details.
explainer.benefit: More complete, cleaner household data and fewer input errors.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Without switching, entry stays as before.

features.title: Brokerage: New Action to Preview Premiums for Draft Policies
features.summary: The new invocable action previewPolicyPremium shows rolled-up premiums for a draft policy hierarchy without saving changes.
features.recommendation: If you use Insurance Brokerage: check whether flows or agents for policy changes should show a premium preview before saving, and add the previewPolicyPremium action.

explainer.what: Brokers want to see how a policy change affects the premium before saving it. There's now a ready-made building block for automations.
explainer.benefit: Premium impact is visible before saving, so fewer corrections.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The building block stays unused.

features.title: Brokerage: New Connect REST APIs for Bulk Policy Processing
features.summary: New REST resources create and complete endorsements, issue policies and reinstate them, all in bulk. There's also a premium preview for draft policies.
features.recommendation: If you run Insurance Brokerage with integrations: check with your developers whether bulk operations (such as annual endorsements or issuing) can run more efficiently through the new bulk resources under /connect/insurance/brokerage/policies.

explainer.what: Brokers often need to change or issue many policies at once. Other systems can now do that in one go through new interfaces.
explainer.benefit: Faster bulk operations and fewer single calls in integrations.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing integrations keep running.

features.title: Brokerage: New Connect in Apex Methods for Policy Operations
features.summary: The ConnectApi.InsuranceBrokerageFamily class gets methods to endorse, issue, cancel and reinstate policies, individually and in bulk, plus a premium preview.
features.recommendation: If you extend Insurance Brokerage with custom Apex: check whether your own logic for endorsements, issuing, cancellation or reinstatement can be replaced by the new ConnectApi methods. That reduces maintenance.

explainer.what: Developers can now code policy operations such as issuing or cancelling policies with ready-made Salesforce building blocks instead of building the logic themselves.
explainer.benefit: Less custom development and more robust policy processes.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Your own code keeps running.

features.title: Fundraising: Field Mappings for Cases and Messaging Subscribers
features.summary: The FieldMappingConfig metadata type supports the new values Case and MessagingSubscriber in the processType field.
features.recommendation: If you use Nonprofit Cloud Fundraising and deploy field mappings as metadata: check whether you need mappings for cases or messaging subscribers and add them to your deployment process.

explainer.what: Nonprofits can now also define which fields are carried over automatically for service requests and messaging contacts, and move that setup between systems.
explainer.benefit: Consistent data transfer for service and messaging processes too.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The change only affects deployments.

features.title: WhatsApp: Service and Utility Messages Consume Credits from November 2, 2026
features.summary: Since November 2, 2026, WhatsApp service messages and utility templates in the 24-hour customer service window consume Salesforce Message Credits; previously they were free there. Inbound messages stay free.
features.recommendation: If you use Enhanced WhatsApp: Meta's pricing change applies automatically since November 2, 2026; no configuration is needed. Check credit consumption for the last few weeks in Digital Wallet, compare it with the WhatsApp rate card (multiplier per country), and replan your budget. Also check whether automated utility templates (such as status updates) can be reduced.

explainer.what: WhatsApp replies to customers used to be free within 24 hours of their last message. Meta now charges for these messages too, and Salesforce deducts credits for them.
explainer.benefit: Knowing your consumption keeps your credit balance from running out unexpectedly.
explainer.ifNothing: The costs apply anyway. Without budget planning, your credits may run out sooner than expected.

features.checkHint: Check Setup > Messaging Settings for Enhanced WhatsApp channels, and Digital Wallet for your credit consumption.

features.title: WhatsApp Templates with a Location Header
features.summary: WhatsApp utility and marketing templates can include a location header that appears as a clickable map for the customer. Agents send them in UCP and Enhanced WhatsApp channels.
features.recommendation: If you use WhatsApp messaging with customer-facing locations (branches, pickup points, service centers): under Messaging Components, create a notification component with External Template format and Location header type, submit it to Meta for approval, and then activate it.

explainer.what: When a customer asks on WhatsApp "Where's your nearest branch?", the rep can send a message with a clickable map instead of just an address.
explainer.benefit: Customers get there faster, with fewer follow-up questions.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Locations keep being sent as text.

features.checkHint: Check Setup > Messaging Settings for WhatsApp channels.

features.title: More Natural WhatsApp Voice Messages from Your AI Agent
features.summary: WhatsApp voice replies from Agentforce sound more natural with better pronunciation. Account, contract and ID numbers are read digit by digit.
features.recommendation: If your Agentforce agent sends voice replies on WhatsApp: nothing to configure. Listen to a few typical replies that contain numbers and check whether texts that spelled out numbers as a workaround can be simplified.

explainer.what: When an AI assistant answers customers with a WhatsApp voice message, it now sounds more natural and reads numbers such as customer numbers clearly digit by digit.
explainer.benefit: Customers understand answers the first time, with fewer follow-up questions.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The improvement arrives automatically.

features.title: Share a WhatsApp Number Across Providers (Meta WAME)
features.summary: With Meta's WhatsApp Account Model Evolution, one number can serve several providers with their own templates and billing. Meta migrates automatically; Salesforce supports only the primary provider role.
features.recommendation: If you use WhatsApp through Salesforce: nothing is needed to keep it running. If you want to share the number with another provider, add Salesforce as the primary partner for the relevant message categories via Embedded Signup in Meta. Note: opt-outs are managed separately by each provider, so align consent or stick to one provider.

explainer.what: Until now, a WhatsApp business number was tied to one provider. Meta now lets you use the same number, for example, for service through Salesforce and for marketing through another provider.
explainer.benefit: More flexibility in choosing providers without a new number.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. WhatsApp keeps working as before after the automatic migration.

features.checkHint: Check Setup > Messaging Settings for WhatsApp channels, and Meta Business Manager for whether the number is shared with other providers.

features.title: RCS as a Service Messaging Channel
features.summary: Customers can start RCS conversations that Omni-Channel routes to service reps in the Service Console or to an Agentforce agent. Previously, RCS was only available for outbound marketing with Marketing Cloud.
features.recommendation: If you use messaging in service and want to reach customers on Android phones via the SMS successor: check the Agentforce Contact Center Digital and RCS add-ons. Then add RCS as a channel in Unified Messaging, procure a verified RCS sender, activate Agent and Bot Conversational Support, and set up Omni-Channel routing.

explainer.what: RCS is the modern successor to SMS, with images, buttons and read receipts. Customers can now also use it for service requests that reach a rep or an AI assistant.
explainer.benefit: Another convenient contact channel for customers, including automation outside business hours.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The channel simply isn't available.

features.checkHint: Check Setup > Company Information for the Agentforce Contact Center Digital and RCS add-on licenses.

features.title: Reply Suggestions as Soon as a Chat Is Transferred
features.summary: When a service rep accepts a conversation from Agentforce or a colleague, two grounded replies and one contextual reply appear right away. The feature is off by default and consumes Flex Credits.
features.recommendation: If you use Agentforce for Service with Einstein Reply Recommendations: under Setup > Service Cloud Einstein > Einstein Reply Recommendations, turn on Proactive Service Replies for a pilot group first. Watch Flex Credit consumption and suggestion quality before rolling it out widely.

explainer.what: When an AI assistant hands a customer chat to a person, that person first has to read the history. Now Salesforce immediately suggests fitting first replies based on the conversation and knowledge articles.
explainer.benefit: Faster first reply after a handoff, so customers wait less.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The feature stays off.

features.checkHint: Check Setup > Service Cloud Einstein > Einstein Reply Recommendations to see whether the feature is available.

features.title: Customer Sentiment in Command Center for Service V2
features.summary: Customer Signals Intelligence shows sentiment (positive, neutral, negative) as a column in the In-Progress Work component of Command Center for Service V2.
features.recommendation: If you use Command Center for Service V2 with Enhanced Omni-Channel and Customer Signals Intelligence or Service Rep Assistant: add the Sentiment column to the In-Progress Work component in Lightning App Builder and show supervisors how to spot critical conversations early.

explainer.what: Customer service team leads now see in their overview, for every ongoing conversation, whether the customer is currently satisfied or upset.
explainer.benefit: Critical conversations stand out earlier, so supervisors can step in in time.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The column stays hidden.

features.checkHint: Check in Setup whether Command Center for Service V2 is turned on and the Customer Signals Intelligence or Service Rep Assistant add-on is licensed.

features.title: Real-Time Sentiment Insights for Voice Calls
features.summary: Customer Signals Intelligence now provides real-time sentiment insights for voice calls too: reps see sentiment shift during the call, supervisors see trends across calls.
features.recommendation: If you use Customer Signals Intelligence with Agentforce for Service and the Service Planner and Adaptive Experience add-ons: set up Service Assistant for Voice first, then turn on the Voice channel under Real-Time Insights in Customer Signals Intelligence Setup and assign the required permission sets (Data Cloud User, Service Planner User and others).

explainer.what: During a customer call, Salesforce shows the rep whether the mood is turning. Team leads see across many calls when things get critical and can plan staffing accordingly.
explainer.benefit: Difficult calls are spotted earlier, and staffing decisions are based on data.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Sentiment insights stay limited to cases and messaging.

features.checkHint: Check Setup > Company Information for Customer Signals Intelligence, Service Planner and Adaptive Experience licenses.

features.title: Document AI for Health: Review Extracted Data Directly on the Record
features.summary: The document extraction request record page has a View button to check extracted values, correct them and add missing values manually. The existing path from the list view remains.
features.recommendation: If you use Document AI for Health: point your case intake team to the new View button on the Document Extract Request page. No setup is needed.

explainer.what: Incoming documents (e.g. medical reports or forms) are read by AI. An employee has to check the results. This can now be done directly on the request's page instead of only from a list.
explainer.benefit: Fewer clicks when checking and completing extracted data.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The existing path from the list view keeps working.

features.title: Document AI for Health: Status Column for Extraction Templates
features.summary: The Extraction Templates table in Document AI for Health now shows whether each template is active or inactive. Only active templates are used during extraction.
features.recommendation: If you use Document AI for Health: check the Status column on the Document AI for Health page in Setup and activate every template that should be used for extraction.

explainer.what: To read documents correctly, the AI needs templates, e.g. for a specific form type. Now you can see at a glance which templates are switched on.
explainer.benefit: Delays caused by templates that are accidentally inactive are spotted faster.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Inactive templates just go unnoticed until an extraction stalls.

features.title: Integrated Care Management: Completed Assessments Show Answered Questions Only
features.summary: When viewing completed internal assessments (Discovery Framework), care managers see only questions with recorded responses, exactly as saved. Previously, visibility rules caused some questions to be missing or blank.
features.recommendation: If you use Integrated Care Management with assessments: let care managers know about the changed view and spot-check one completed assessment. No setup is needed.

explainer.what: Care staff fill in questionnaires about patients. When someone later looked at a finished questionnaire, some questions were blank or missing. Now only answered questions appear, complete and in the right structure.
explainer.benefit: Faster and more reliable review of patient information.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The improvement applies automatically.
