features.title: Referral Management: Guided Setup for Document AI
features.summary: Document AI for Health can be configured in Referral Management with a guided setup. The AI extracts information from incoming faxes and automates referral intake.
features.recommendation: If you still enter referrals manually from faxes and have the Agentforce for Health Cloud license: in Setup, go to Referral Management Settings and follow the guided steps in the External Referral Intake section.

explainer.what: Practices and hospitals often still send referrals by fax. Until now, someone typed in the details. The AI can read them, and setting this up now walks you through it step by step.
explainer.benefit: Less manual typing for the team that handles incoming referrals.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Referrals continue to be captured as today.

features.title: Referral Management: Guided Setup for Predictive Scoring
features.summary: An enhanced guided setup helps you set up predictive scoring for Clinical Service Requests in Health Cloud. It highlights the required configuration tasks and links to related help.
features.recommendation: If you want to introduce predictive scoring for referrals (requires Agentforce for Health Cloud and Data Cloud licenses): in Setup, go to Referral Management Settings and follow the Set Up Referral Predictive Scoring step.

explainer.what: With many incoming referrals, a score helps decide which ones to handle first. Setting up this score now guides you more clearly through all required steps.
explainer.benefit: Faster setup with fewer mistakes.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The feature stays unused or is set up as before.

features.title: Digital Health Insurance: Guided Flow for Medicare Enrollments
features.summary: A flow guides sales reps through selling Medicare plans, including Scope of Appointment consent, formulary and network checks, consultation booking and signature.
features.recommendation: Only relevant if you sell Medicare plans in the US: turn on Digital Insurance, Data Pipelines, Person Accounts, Provider Search and Salesforce Scheduler, then add the Medicare Sales Flow action to the Person Account page. Users need the Use Medicare Sales permission.

explainer.what: Medicare is the US public health insurance for seniors. Selling these plans involves many mandatory steps. A guided assistant now leads the conversation from disclaimer to signature.
explainer.benefit: Faster enrollments in peak season and fewer compliance mistakes.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Irrelevant for orgs that don't sell US Medicare plans.

features.checkHint: Only for Medicare sales in the US; requires Digital Insurance Policy/Product Admin licenses

features.title: Life Sciences Event Management: Sync Expenses with Concur
features.summary: Event expenses can be synchronized two-way with Concur expense reports via MuleSoft, including offline on the iPad.
features.recommendation: If you use Event Management in Life Sciences Cloud and SAP Concur: check whether the MuleSoft Concur Expense Sync template can replace the double reconciliation of event costs.

explainer.what: Pharma field teams organize events with physicians, and the costs end up in an expense system (Concur). Until now this was entered twice. Now both systems sync automatically.
explainer.benefit: No double entry and reconciliation of event costs.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Costs continue to be maintained separately.

features.title: Life Sciences Order Management: Note on Scope and Additional Costs
features.summary: Order Management for Agentforce Life Sciences includes only Orders and Pricing. Salesforce clarifies that other Order Management features (e.g. Billing) can increase subscription costs.
features.recommendation: If you roll out Order Management in Life Sciences Cloud: clarify costs with your Salesforce account executive before using additional features such as Billing.

explainer.what: Field reps can enter orders for pharmacies and have prices calculated. Salesforce added that only these parts are included. If you also use invoicing, for example, you may pay more.
explainer.benefit: No surprises on your next license bill.
explainer.ifNothing: Using features that aren't included can lead to higher subscription costs.

features.title: Life Sciences: Custom Time Off Territory Categories
features.summary: Time off territory categories such as company celebration days, training or regulatory duties can be configured freely. Rules define whether other activities can be scheduled alongside them.
features.recommendation: If you use Time Off Territory: in the Admin Console, go to Time Off Territory, create your own downtime categories and define rules for which of them allow parallel activities.

explainer.what: Field reps aren't with customers every day, e.g. because of training or company events. These absences can now be grouped by your own company rules, including whether visits are still allowed on the same day.
explainer.benefit: Fewer scheduling conflicts and planning in line with company policy.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The standard categories remain.

features.title: Life Sciences: Capture Only Samples and Marketing Items per Group Visit Attendee
features.summary: The Attendee Visit Engagement page can show only the Samples, Direct to Practitioner and Marketing Items sidebars. Product details from the parent visit apply to all attendees automatically.
features.recommendation: If your field reps record group visits: in the Admin Console, go to Visit Administration and turn on Capture only samples and marketing items per attendee, if your requirements allow it.

explainer.what: For a visit with several physicians, field reps used to enter a lot per person. Now the products discussed apply to everyone, and only samples and marketing items are recorded per person.
explainer.benefit: Less data entry and consistent data for group visits.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Data entry stays as it is.

features.title: Life Sciences: Twilio Remote Sessions Now on the Desktop Site
features.summary: Field users can run remote sessions with healthcare professionals via Twilio on the desktop site, including presentations, attendee controls and signatures. Previously this was only available in the mobile app.
features.recommendation: If you use Remote Engagement with Twilio or want to replace external video tools: test desktop use with a pilot team and check that the Twilio setup for Remote Engagement is complete.

explainer.what: Pharma reps often talk to physicians by video instead of in person. Until now, this only worked on the iPad. Now it works on the computer too, and the physician joins via a secure link without an app.
explainer.benefit: No switching to external video tools; presentation data and signatures go straight to the visit.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Remote sessions remain limited to the mobile app.

features.title: Life Sciences: Sign Consent in Remote Sessions on Smartphones
features.summary: Healthcare professionals who join a remote session on their phone can now review consent topics, opt in or out and sign electronically. Previously this required a laptop or desktop.
features.recommendation: If you use remote signatures: let field reps know that consent can now be captured from participants on smartphones. The release note doesn't describe any setup steps.

explainer.what: Before a pharma company may contact a physician, e.g. by email, it needs their consent. The physician can now sign it on their phone during a video meeting.
explainer.benefit: More consents captured without a follow-up meeting or switching channels.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Smartphone consent simply goes unused.

features.title: Life Sciences: Resolve GraphQL Queries Offline in Custom LSC Apps
features.summary: When the iPad is offline, the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app resolves GraphQL queries from custom LWCs against the data synced to the device.
features.recommendation: If you build custom LSC apps (LWC) for the mobile app: turn on offline support and build queries with the graphql wire adapter from lightning/uiGraphQLApi. Check existing components for offline readiness.

explainer.what: Field reps are often in buildings without a connection. Custom-built screens in the app then sometimes stopped working. Now they get their data from the device's storage.
explainer.benefit: Custom extensions stay usable without a network connection.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Custom components using GraphQL stay limited offline.

features.title: Life Sciences: Combine Multiple Components in a Single LSC App
features.summary: An LSC app on the Home Page or a record page tab in the mobile app can now contain multiple nested custom LWCs. Components can be reused across several apps.
features.recommendation: If you build custom LSC apps: create a parent LWC with the lscMobileInline_ prefix and a targets entry, then nest child components inside it. Check whether existing single-component apps can be merged this way.

explainer.what: Companies build their own screens for the field app. Until now, only one building block was allowed per spot. Now lists, cards or menus can be combined and reused.
explainer.benefit: Richer custom apps with less duplicate development work.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. It stays at one component per LSC app.

features.title: Life Sciences Event Management: Event Type from the Record Type
features.summary: With event type mappings, a managed event is classified automatically based on its record type instead of entering the same information twice.
features.recommendation: If you use Event Management: in the Admin Console, open the Event Management tile and create event type mappings per record type. This avoids conflicting values in reports.

explainer.what: When creating an event, you choose a kind (e.g. training) and had to enter the event type as well. Now Salesforce fills it in automatically.
explainer.benefit: Fewer clicks and more reliable reporting.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The event type continues to be maintained manually.

features.title: Life Sciences Event Management: Fill Participant Type and Role Automatically
features.summary: Participant type mappings now apply to any Managed Event Participant record type. Participant type, role and type-role mapping fields are populated automatically.
features.recommendation: If you use Event Management with custom participant record types: in the Admin Console, open the Event Management tile and create participant type mappings.

explainer.what: At events, participants (e.g. speaker, guest) are recorded with a type and role. This used to take several steps; now choosing the record type is enough.
explainer.benefit: Faster data entry with fewer errors.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Type and role continue to be entered separately.

features.title: Life Sciences: Capture Interactions Within Presentation Pages
features.summary: With the trackInteraction function in HTML slides, you can capture taps, clicks and video plays per presentation page, including account and visit context.
features.recommendation: If you use HTML presentations in the field: agree with your content agency which interactions to capture with PresentationPlayer.trackInteraction(), and add custom fields to the presentation click stream entry object if needed.

explainer.what: Pharma reps show physicians presentations on the iPad. Until now, you only saw which pages were viewed. Now you also see whether a video was started or a button was tapped.
explainer.benefit: A better basis for improving content in a targeted way.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Page views remain the only metric.

features.title: Life Sciences: Track Email Fragment Usage Across the Field Team
features.summary: Sending an email creates a record for each included fragment, capturing its version and content. This gives an auditable view of which fragments reps send to healthcare professionals.
features.recommendation: If you use field email with fragments: in the Admin Console, go to Email > Email Settings and turn on Track email fragment usage. For the mobile app, set up the object metadata cache for Life Science Email Fragment and Email Template Fragment as described in the release note.

explainer.what: Field reps build emails to physicians from approved text blocks. Now the system records which block was sent in which version.
explainer.benefit: An auditable communication history and a way to measure which content works.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Fragment usage stays invisible.

features.title: Life Sciences: Work Faster in the Content Library and Presentation Player
features.summary: Inquiries and surveys can be started directly from the presentation player, and on desktop also per attendee. The mobile app shows four thumbnails per row, and slides can be reordered with drag handles.
features.recommendation: If you use Intelligent Content: in the Admin Console, configure the Inquiry and Survey quick actions and select the Intelligent Content location for each.

explainer.what: During a presentation to a physician, the rep can now start an inquiry or survey without leaving the presentation. Picking content on the iPad is also clearer.
explainer.benefit: Smoother conversations and less switching between screens.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The visual improvements arrive automatically; the actions stay off.

features.title: Life Sciences Mobile: Automatically Select the Best Opted-In Email
features.summary: The mobile app automatically selects the best opted-in email address and orders recipients like on desktop, based on the preference rank of contact point emails.
features.recommendation: If you use field email in the mobile app: check that the preference rank is maintained on contact point email records, because the automatic selection relies on it.

explainer.what: Many physicians have several email addresses. The app now automatically picks the preferred address that has consent.
explainer.benefit: More emails reach the right address; the same behavior on iPad and desktop.
explainer.ifNothing: The new selection applies automatically; without a rank, addresses are sorted alphabetically.

features.title: Life Sciences Data Kit: New Data Streams for Email Fragments and Presentations
features.summary: The Life Sciences Data Kit adds a new data model object and data stream for email fragments. Email message and presentation click stream mappings now cover send status, consent and in-content interactions.
features.recommendation: If you use Life Sciences Cloud with Data 360: deploy the updated Life Sciences Data Kit and check whether your existing email and presentation data streams should adopt the new mappings. You need the Life Sciences Commercial Admin, Data Cloud Architect and Data Cloud User permission sets.

explainer.what: Data 360 collects customer data from different sources for analysis. Now details about sent email fragments and clicks inside presentations flow there too.
explainer.benefit: A fuller picture of how physicians respond to content, as a basis for analytics and segments.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The new data just won't reach Data 360.

features.title: Life Sciences: New and Changed Objects and Fields
features.summary: New objects and fields for Life Sciences, including DowntimeCategory on TerritoryUserDowntime, the LifeScienceEmailFragment object, MetricEntryType on PresentationClickStrmEntry and many quote and store check fields for Order Management.
features.recommendation: If you use Life Sciences Cloud: review the new fields for the areas you use (Time Off Territory, Intelligent Content, Order Management) and add them to layouts, reports and permission sets as needed.

explainer.what: Salesforce added new data fields, e.g. a category for field team absences or shipping and billing addresses on quotes. For employees to see them, the admin often has to add them first.
explainer.benefit: New features can be fully used and reported on.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. The new fields stay hidden and unused.

features.title: Unified Catalog: More Options for Intake Forms and Service Requests
features.summary: Intake form attributes can be renamed, Long Text Area attributes added, and required and optional products attached to catalog requests. Service Request records show open activities and related knowledge articles.
features.recommendation: If you use Unified Catalog: review your intake forms. Clearer field labels (e.g. Request Title instead of Subject), a long text field for justifications and required products can reduce follow-up questions.

explainer.what: Employees order things like laptops or access through an internal catalog. The order forms can now be tailored better, and fulfillers see help articles and open tasks right on the request.
explainer.benefit: More complete requests and faster fulfillment.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Forms and requests stay as they are.

features.checkHint: Only with Unified Catalog

features.title: Nonprofit Cloud: Participant Portal Template for Program Management
features.summary: The new Program Participant Portal Experience Cloud template gives participants self-service access to programs, applications, enrollments, benefits and referrals. Salesforce clarified that it's available only for Nonprofit Cloud.
features.recommendation: If you use Program Management with Track Applications in Nonprofit Cloud and have the Program and Case Management for Experience Cloud add-on: create a site in Experience Builder with the Program Participant Portal template, adjust the branding and pilot it with a few participants.

explainer.what: Nonprofits support people through programs, such as counseling or assistance offers. With the portal, participants check their applications and benefits online themselves instead of calling.
explainer.benefit: Fewer routine inquiries to staff and more time for the actual work.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Participants keep contacting staff directly.

features.title: Fundraising: Create Households During Gift Entry
features.summary: In the Gift Entry Grid or via the Business Process API, donors (person accounts) can be added to a new household directly. Only in Nonprofit Cloud with the Automatic Household Creation and Naming add-on.
features.recommendation: If you use Fundraising with the Automatic Household Creation and Naming add-on: point gift officers to the Auto Create Household option and review custom automation for household creation that may become redundant. For integrations, use the shouldAutoCreateHousehold parameter.

explainer.what: Fundraising organizations often group donors into households, such as a married couple. Until now, the household had to be created separately. Now a checkbox does it right during gift entry.
explainer.benefit: Less manual work and complete donor data from the first entry.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Households continue to be created separately.

features.title: Stage Management: Pull Future Steps Forward with Run Now
features.summary: Planned steps from a later stage can be pulled forward and completed early. Previously you had to wait for the stage or work outside the plan.
features.recommendation: If you use Stage Management (e.g. for origination or underwriting): point teams to the Run Now action in the Record Stage Overview component and agree which steps may be pulled forward.

explainer.what: Some processes, such as a loan review, run in fixed stages. Now an employee can complete a step from a later stage whenever they have time.
explainer.benefit: Shorter cycle times through parallel work.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Steps keep running strictly one after another.

features.checkHint: Only with Stage Management

features.title: Public Sector: Authorize Services and Track Delivery
features.summary: Agencies can authorize services such as court translators, expert witnesses or nursing support with Service Authorization and track delivery. Delivery records link to claim adjudication to validate invoices.
features.recommendation: If you engage third-party providers in Agentforce Public Sector: check whether Service Authorization and Service Delivery can replace your current approval and invoice checks, including a portal view of unclaimed units for providers.

explainer.what: Agencies hire external experts, such as translators for court hearings. Now the system records what was approved and what was actually delivered, and invoices are checked against it.
explainer.benefit: Traceable billing and fewer payments for services that weren't delivered.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Approvals and billing continue as before.

features.title: Public Sector: Customizable Claims Forms and AI Invoice Extraction
features.summary: Claims submission forms in Experience Cloud can be adapted with custom fields. Uploaded invoices are read with Unstructured Document Processing, filling claim fields and line items.
features.recommendation: If providers submit claims through a portal: adapt the form fields to your requirements (e.g. authorization number, cost center) and define in Setup, via a JSON schema, which fields are extracted from invoices.

explainer.what: Providers submit invoices to an agency. The forms can now be tailored to the agency, and AI reads amounts, dates and line items from the uploaded invoice.
explainer.benefit: Less typing for providers and case workers, cleaner data for review.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Claims continue to be captured with the standard form.

features.title: Tax and Revenue Management: Taxpayer 360 Profile with a Data Kit
features.summary: The new Taxpayer 360 data model combines identity, household, income, filing status and payment history in one view. New: the Tax and Revenue Management Data Kit for Data 360.
features.recommendation: If you use Tax and Revenue Management with Data 360: configure a data space, deploy the Tax and Revenue Management Data Kit and load the remaining data with manual data streams via a CRM connector. Your existing system stays the source of record.

explainer.what: Tax agencies often keep taxpayer data in several systems. The new data model shows everything about a person at a glance without replacing the legacy systems.
explainer.benefit: Case workers switch between systems less often and answer faster.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Data stays spread across systems.

features.title: Tax and Revenue Management: New Connect REST and Apex Methods
features.summary: New resources return the logged-in taxpayer's filings, documents, payments, refunds and assessments for a tax year, plus a profile with the tax years that have filings. The endpoint URLs were updated.
features.recommendation: If you build a taxpayer portal on Tax and Revenue Management: check whether the new …/tax-revenue/tax-account/activities and …/profile resources (or ConnectApi.MissionforceTaxRevenueApi) can replace custom queries. Compare any endpoint URLs you already use with the updated release note.

explainer.what: Taxpayers want to see online what they filed, paid or got refunded. Developers can now get this information through ready-made interfaces.
explainer.benefit: Less custom development for portals and apps.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Custom queries keep working.

features.title: Tax and Revenue Management: New Flow Actions for Taxpayer Profile and Activity
features.summary: The new invocable actions getTaxpayerProfile and getTaxpayerActivity return the logged-in taxpayer's profile, tax years and activity (filings, documents, payments, refunds, assessments) in flows.
features.recommendation: If you build flows for a taxpayer portal: check whether getTaxpayerProfile and getTaxpayerActivity can replace custom queries or Apex.

explainer.what: Flows are click-based automations. Tax portals now get ready-made building blocks that fetch a citizen's profile and tax-year overview without code.
explainer.benefit: Portal features can be built without custom code.
explainer.ifNothing: Nothing. Existing flows keep running.

features.title: GPT-5 Family and o3/o3-pro Rerouted on December 11, 2026
features.summary: Starting December 11, 2026, requests to GPT-5, GPT-5-Pro, o3 and o3-pro go to GPT-5.6-Sol, GPT-5-Mini to GPT-5.6-Terra and GPT-5-Nano to GPT-5.6-Luna. Responses may change as a result.
features.recommendation: Deadline December 11, 2026: check in Prompt Builder and AI Models whether prompt templates or models use GPT-5, GPT-5-Mini, GPT-5-Nano, GPT-5-Pro, o3 or o3-pro. Test them now with the respective successor (GPT-5.6-Sol, -Terra or -Luna) and adjust prompts if responses change.
features.checkHint: Only relevant if prompt templates or models use the GPT-5 family or o3/o3-pro. Check in Setup > Prompt Builder or Einstein Studio > AI Models.

explainer.what: Salesforce is retiring some older AI models from OpenAI and automatically redirecting requests to newer models.
explainer.benefit: The new models are more current. Testing beforehand avoids surprises in the results.
explainer.ifNothing: The rerouting happens anyway. Prompts tuned to an old model may then produce different or worse answers.
